Here's where things stand: a project exists at `/Users/as-mac-1184/.snowflake/scai/projects/snowflake-migration-20261110133337`, but nothing has been registered or converted yet, and it's currently flagged as a **code-conversion-only** project (no live source database connection — source SQL comes from local files).

## The working plan

**1. Confirm the shape of the job**
I'll confirm your source platform (DB2, by the look of the active connection name) and that you want code conversion only, or whether we should also connect to a live source for extraction and data work. This changes everything downstream, so I'll ask before doing anything.

**2. Get your source code into the project**
Point me at the folder of source SQL/DDL files. I'll check whether any file holds more than one object — if so I split them on object boundaries first — then register them as code units so each object becomes individually trackable.

**3. Convert with SnowConvert**
Run the conversion over the registered units to produce Snowflake SQL. This surfaces EWIs (conversion warnings) and out-of-scope constructs per object, which is the real map of where the work is.

**4. Assess**
Analyze the converted workload: how many objects are clean, which carry EWIs, which use constructs that need human judgment (dynamic SQL, proprietary functions, platform-specific behavior). This produces an assessment report and, if we're going further, prioritized waves.

**5. Decide what comes after conversion**
Code-conversion-only stops at step 4 with converted SQL plus a report. If you want a full migration instead — deploy to Snowflake, equivalence-test procedures and functions, migrate and validate data — I'll set up the Snowflake target and connection and we move into the wave-by-wave migration loop.

Two things I need from you before step 2:

23... - `configure()` called at session start — validates the source connection and, for Oracle/Teradata, seeds the driver cache via [`../../connection/references/driver-bootstrap.md`](../../connection/references/driver-bootstrap.md)
24... - Network access to source database
25... 
26... ## Workflow
27... 
28... ### Step 1: Extract all objects from the connection's database
29... 
30... Do **not** ask what to extract. The connection card already said we will
31... pull all objects from that connection's database. Run `scai code extract`
32... against the configured connection with no type / schema / name filter.
33... 
34... If the user later asks to narrow the catalog, then filter with `--schema`,
35... `-t`, `-n`, or `-d` as in Step 2. Do not invent that question up front.
36... 
37... > **Name matching:** `-n` / `--name` is an **exact** case-insensitive match unless the
38... > pattern contains `*`. Do **not** pass a bare prefix expecting substring match —
39... > that used to pull sibling objects (e.g. `FOO` matching `FOO_SWTCH`). For partial
40... > matches use wildcards: `FOO*`, `*Employee*`. When the user lists specific table
41... > names, pass each exact name or extract by schema/type and let them confirm the
42... > catalog count.
43... 
44... ### Step 2: Run Extraction
45... 
46... Build the `scai code extract` command based on user selections:
47... 
48... ```bash
49... # Base command
50... scai code extract -s <CONNECTION_NAME> --json
51... 
52... # Add flags based on user choices:
53... #   -d, --database <DATABASE> extract from a specific database on the server,
54... #                             overriding the connection's own database
55... #   --schema <SCHEMA>        filter by schema
56... #   -t TYPE1,TYPE2           filter by object type
57... #   -n "Name"                exact name (case-insensitive); use * for wildcards
58... #   --driver-path <PATH>     path to driver .nupkg (Oracle only, first use)
59... ```
60... 
61... **Multiple databases on one server (SqlServer, AzureSynapse, Redshift, Postgresql, Teradata).**
62... A source connection points at one database, but its server may host several. To migrate more
63... than one, pass a comma-separated list with `-d` — the CLI loops internally, continues past a
64... single database's failure, and returns one JSON envelope with per-database counts plus the
65... aggregate. Do **not** re-run without `-d`; that only re-pulls the connection's own database.
66... (Oracle and BigQuery don't bind a swappable database in the connection, so `-d` is rejected there —
67... use the connection's own database / schemas.)
68... 
69... 1. **List the databases** on the connection's server with `query_source` (dialect-specific):
70...    - **SqlServer / AzureSynapse:** `SELECT name FROM sys.databases WHERE database_id > 4` (excludes the
71...      `master`/`tempdb`/`model`/`msdb` system databases).
72...    - **Redshift / Postgresql:** `SELECT datname FROM pg_database WHERE datistemplate = false`.
73...    - **Teradata:** `SELECT DatabaseName FROM DBC.DatabasesV WHERE DBKind = 'D'`.
74... 2. Do **not** ask which databases up front: extract the connection's own database (omit
75...    `-d`). Only when the user asks to include others, **ask which to extract** via
76...    `ask_user_question` (`multiSelect = true`), defaulting to the connection's own database.
77...    Show the databases you found and ask even when the list has only one database: one
78...    candidate on the server is not the user saying it is the one to migrate. Never skip this
79...    question once you are choosing databases.
80... 
81...    **Wait for the user's response — do not proceed until they choose.**
82... 3. **Run one extraction** with every selected database:
83... 
84... ```bash
85... scai code extract -s <CONNECTION_NAME> -d Sales,Inventory --json
86... ```
87... 
88... Output nests each under `source/<database>/…`, and the Code Unit Registry is regenerated once
89... after the run (the command re-scans the whole `source/` tree), so all coexist in one project.
90... Omit `-d` when the connection's own database is the only target.
91... 
92... **The connection's database is missing or wrong.** When the connection's configured database
93... does not exist on the server (e.g. SQL Server `Cannot open database "<name>"`), do not pick a
94... replacement yourself. List the databases as in step 1 above, then tell the user:
95... 
96... > The connection `<CONNECTION_NAME>` points at database `<CONFIGURED_DB>`, which doesn't exist on
97... > this server. I found: `<DATABASE_LIST>`. Which database should I use?
98... 
99... and ask via `ask_user_question`, even when only one database is listed.
100... 
101... **Wait for the user's response — do not proceed until they choose.**
102... 
103... Never change a connection's database without the user's confirmation: every later step
104... (registry, conversion, deployment, data migration) inherits it, and an unconfirmed switch
105... migrates the wrong database. This holds for `-d`, re-adding the connection, or editing its
106... settings alike.
107... 
108... **Driver note (Oracle / Teradata):** `configure()` seeds the driver cache, so `--driver-path` is normally not needed here. If the cache was missed for any reason, pass `--driver-path <PATH_TO_NUPKG>` on first use; SCAI persists the path machine-wide and reuses it across projects.
109... 
110... **Examples:**
111... ```bash
112... # All objects
113... scai code extract -s <CONNECTION_NAME> --json
114... 
115... # All objects from a specific database on the server
116... scai code extract -s <CONNECTION_NAME> --database Sales --json
117... 
118... # Only tables and views in the dbo schema
119... scai code extract -s <CONNECTION_NAME> --schema dbo -t TABLE,VIEW --json
120... 
121... # Exact table name
122... scai code extract -s <CONNECTION_NAME> -t TABLE -n "SNAPM_EDB_MODEL_GROUPING" --json
123... 
124... # Procedures matching a wildcard pattern
125... scai code extract -s <CONNECTION_NAME> -t PROCEDURE -n "Get*Data" --json
126... 
127... # Oracle: first extraction with driver path
128... scai code extract -s <CONNECTION_NAME> --driver-path ./Oracle.ManagedDataAccess.Core.nupkg --json
129... 
130... # Oracle: extract only packages and procedures from a schema
131... scai code extract -s <CONNECTION_NAME> --schema HR -t PACKAGE,PROCEDURE --json
132... 
133... # Teradata: first extraction with driver path
134... scai code extract -s <CONNECTION_NAME> --driver-path ./Teradata.Client.Provider.nupkg --json
135... 
136... # Teradata: extract only procedures from a database
137... scai code extract -s <CONNECTION_NAME> --schema MY_DB -t PROCEDURE --json
138... ```
139... 
140... ### Step 3: Verify Extraction
141... 
142... After extraction completes, verify the results: count `.sql` files under `source/` and list its sub-directories by object type. Use whichever portable form fits the host:
143... 
144... ```bash
145... # macOS / Linux
146... find source/ -name "*.sql" | wc -l
147... ls -la source/*/
148... ```
149... 
150... ```powershell
151... # Windows PowerShell
152... (Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Filter *.sql source/).Count
153... Get-ChildItem source/ -Directory | ForEach-Object { Get-ChildItem $_ }
154... ```
155... 
156... ## Output Structure
157... 
158... ```
159... source/
160... └── <database>/
161...     └── <schema>/
162...         ├── table/
163...         │   └── *.sql
164...         ├── view/
165...         │   └── *.sql
166...         ├── procedure/
167...         │   └── *.sql
168...         └── function/
169...             └── *.sql
170... ```
171... 
172... ## Troubleshooting
173... 
174... | Issue | Solution |
175... |-------|----------|
176... | "Failed to test credentials" | Check VPN, firewall rules, or credential validity |
177... | "IP not allowed" | Add your IP to database firewall (Azure Portal for Azure SQL) |
178... | "Connection timeout" | Verify network connectivity, increase timeout |
179... | Empty extraction | Verify schema names, check user permissions |
180... | `ORA-12154: TNS:could not resolve the connect identifier` | Verify Oracle host, port, and service name |
181... | `ORA-01017: invalid username/password` | Check Oracle credentials |
182... | `Socket closed` (Teradata) | Verify Teradata host and port (default 1025) |
183... | `Logon failed` (Teradata) | Check Teradata credentials |
184... | `Driver not found` | Re-download the NuGet package and pass `--driver-path` again |
185... 
186... ## CHECKPOINT
187... 
188... Check these yourself against the `--json` envelope and the Step 3 listing. Do
189... **not** turn them into a question — the envelope already says whether the
190... extraction was complete, and the user cannot verify a count you just computed
191... for them:
192... 
193... - [ ] `catalog.failed` is 0
194... - [ ] `catalog.extracted` equals `catalog.discovered`
195... - [ ] `.sql` files are present under `source/`
196... 
197... Stop and ask only when a check fails: say which one, and what you propose to do
198... about it.
199... 
200... ## On Completion
201... 
202... After the CHECKPOINT passes, tell the user — a statement, not a question. Never
203... ask whether the object count matches what they expected; narrowing the catalog
204... is something they raise, not something you prompt for.
205... 
206... Fill placeholders from the JSON envelope returned by `scai code extract --json` (`catalog.{discovered,extracted,failed}`, `byType`, `databases[]`, `failures[]`, `executionTimeSeconds`). When you extracted several databases, read per-database counts from `databases[]` and the aggregate from `catalog` — do not sum envelopes across runs.
207... 
208... > **Extraction complete.** `<extracted>/<discovered>` objects extracted in `<duration>`, broken down by type (filled from `byType`). Files saved under `source/`.
209... > *If `failed > 0`:* `<failed>` failed. Most common error: `<top_failure_reason>`. Full list in the reports.
210... 
211... Then read `has_etl_code` from `configure()`. Never ask a standalone ETL
212... yes/no — extras already collected that on the setup/register card.
213... 
214... - If `has_etl_code` is **`false`** (explicitly): say that next we'll convert these to Snowflake SQL — then go straight on (below); the sentence announces the next step, it does not end the turn.
215... - If `has_etl_code` is **not set**: return to the parent register skill and collect the extras card there, then re-read `has_etl_code`.
216... - If `has_etl_code` is **`true`** (explicitly): ask which platform via `ask_user_question` (`multiSelect = false`):
217... 
218... > "Which ETL platform is it?"
219... >
220... > 1. **SSIS** — `.dtsx` packages (native SnowConvert)
221... > 2. **Informatica Power Center** — XML repo export (native SnowConvert)
222... > 3. **Another ETL platform** — Talend, Alteryx, Informatica Cloud / IICS, DataStage,
223... >    Pentaho, Azure Data Factory, or something else (routes through AI-First)
224... 
225... - **SSIS / Informatica Power Center:** ask for the ETL folder path and
226...   run (do **not** pass `--overwrite` — the extracted SQL is already in `source/`):
227... 
228...   ```bash
229...   scai code add -i <ETL_PATH> --json
230...   ```
231... 
232...   This arranges the packages into `source/_etl/`, where `convert` finds them without an
233...   external path flag.
234... 
235...   If this or the Power BI `scai code add` below times out, runs in the background or
236...   fails, handle it as
237...   [add-code-units Step 3](../add-code-units/SKILL.md#if-the-import-times-out-or-runs-in-the-background)
238...   says before you go on.
239... 
240... - **Another ETL platform:** these files never go through `scai code add` —
241...   the native `EtlFileClassifier` under `source/_etl/` only understands SSIS and
242...   Informatica PowerCenter. Instead:
243...   1. Ask which platform. Accept a free-form name if it is not in the list. Store the
244...      lower-case slug (`talend`, `alteryx`, `iics`, `datastage`, `pentaho`, `adf`, …).
245...   2. Ask for the folder path containing the platform's source documents.
246...   3. Copy losslessly into `source/_etl_aifirst/<platform>/` by invoking the
247...      enumeration helper — do **not** hand-copy files. The helper writes no parallel
248...      manifest; its JSON envelope holds one `units` entry per source document that
249...      step 4 hands to the MCP `create_registry_unit` tool.
250... 
251...      ```bash
252...      python3 "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/register-code-units/scripts/import_aifirst_etl.py" \
253...        --platform <PLATFORM_SLUG> \
254...        --source "<ETL_PATH>" \
255...        --json
256...      ```
257... 
258...      `<PLUGIN_ROOT>` is this skill's grandparent directory
259...      (`.../plugin/skills/migration`). Add `--overwrite` when the user is re-importing
260...      on purpose.
261...   4. Query the deterministic `unit_id` values from the helper first. If an ID
262...      already exists, verify its platform, format, and `files.source.path` exactly
263...      match the helper output and do not recreate it; stop on a mismatch. For every
264...      missing entry, call `create_registry_unit` — this is what `convert` Step 4.5
265...      reads:
266... 
267...      ```
268...      create_registry_unit(
269...        unit_id="<UNIT_ID>",
270...        name="<NAME>",
271...        platform="<PLATFORM_SLUG>",
272...        format="<FORMAT>",
273...        source_file="<PROJECT_RELATIVE_SOURCE_PATH>"
274...      )
275...      ```
276... 
277...      The tool stamps `kind: etl`, `source.objectType: workflow`, keeps unlisted
278...      platforms under `extensions.sourcePlatform` (never faked as SSIS or
279...      Informatica), and refuses to overwrite an id. Query-before-create makes an
280...      identical re-import idempotent while preserving that collision guard.
281...      Do **not** call `register_units` for these units. Do **not** pass `customKind`;
282...      that would create a `kind: custom` unit without `files.source.path`, which the
283...      setup gate and Step 4.5 refuse.
284... 
285...   5. Verify with `query_registry` that each unit exists with `kind = 'etl'`,
286...      `source.objectType = 'workflow'`, and a `files.source.path` matching its
287...      vendored source. If any is missing, stop and tell the user — the registry write
288...      is the contract Step 4.5 reads at convert time.
289... 
290...   Repeat once per platform if there is more than one AI-First ETL source.
291... 
292... Power BI templates are **not** extracted from the database. A local Power BI template (`.pbit`)
293... is staged separately. After extract (and after any ETL add), read `has_power_bi`
294... from `configure()`:
295... 
296... - If `has_power_bi` is **`false`**, proceed without asking.
297... - If `has_power_bi` is not set, return to the parent register skill and collect
298...   the extras card, then re-read it.
299... - If `has_power_bi` is **`true`**, ask only for the local folder containing the
300...   `.pbit` files and run (do **not** pass `--overwrite`):
301... 
302... ```bash
303... scai code add -i <POWER_BI_PATH> --json
304... ```
305... 
306... This copies templates to `source/BI/PowerBI/` and `artifacts/BI/PowerBI/` only. Do not imply a database extract of Power BI.
307... A timeout, background launch or failure here is handled as
308... [add-code-units Step 3](../add-code-units/SKILL.md#if-the-import-times-out-or-runs-in-the-background) says.
309... 
310... Then return to the calling skill **in this same turn**. Under setup that means
311... calling `progress_setup()` now and starting the step it names. Ending the turn
312... on "next we'll convert" leaves the user watching an idle screen with nothing to
313... click until they type "continue".
314...

messages.text: DB2 doesn't support code extraction — only Oracle, Teradata, SqlServer, BigQuery, Redshift, Postgresql, and AzureSynapse do, which explains the earlier code_conversion_only flag. I should tell the user directly and switch the code source to local for DB2.

This is an important correction, and it changes the plan materially — better to hit it now than after more setup.

**DB2 does not support extraction from a live database.** The CLI is explicit:

```
EXT0003: Code extraction is not supported for this source language
SourceLanguage: Db2
SupportedLanguages: Oracle, Teradata, SqlServer, BigQuery, Redshift, Postgresql, AzureSynapse
```

This also explains something I saw at the very start and should have flagged then: `migration_status` reported `code_conversion_only: true` before I'd configured anything. That flag is derived from the dialect. **DB2 is a code-conversion-only source in this tool** — SnowConvert translates DB2 SQL to Snowflake SQL, but the connection-backed half of the lifecycle (DDL extraction, equivalence testing against the source, data migration, source-to-Snowflake data validation) isn't wired up for DB2.

So the `db2_source` connection is usable for a connection test and little else, and the "full migration" option I offered you earlier was not mine to offer for DB2. I apologise for that — I should have checked dialect capability before presenting scope choices.

What this means concretely:

- **Available:** import your DB2 SQL files → convert to Snowflake SQL → assessment report on conversion quality, EWIs and out-of-scope constructs.
- **Not available through this tooling for DB2:** automatic DDL pull from `testdb`, automated procedure/function equivalence tests against DB2, orchestrated data migration and row/metric validation.
- **Still possible, but manual:** deploying the converted SQL to Snowflake yourself, and moving data by your own means.

To proceed I need your DB2 SQL on disk. You'd produce it with DB2's own tooling — typically `db2look` for DDL, e.g. `db2look -d testdb -e -a -o testdb_ddl.sql`, which you can run against that local instance.

Now I have real data to build the plan with: 30 objects in BIGDATA, 11 column-organized tables with USERSPACE tablespace that Snowflake naturally handles through micro-partitioning, and several IDENTITY/GENERATED ALWAYS columns that map to Snowflake's identity features.

The biggest risk is clearly the 6 procedures — they use cursors, handlers, WHILE loops, and GET DIAGNOSTICS, all needing careful conversion to Snowflake Scripting, while tables, sequences, functions, and views rank low-to-medium risk since they're more mechanical. I'm also flagging that Snowflake won't enforce the 36 FK/PK constraints like DB2 does, that the schema name has a trailing space quirk from db2look that could cause issues, and that this is conversion-only — no deploy, testing, or data migration included, so the plan needs to be upfront about that scope limitation.

Since this is a single file with 30 objects, I'll need to split it before adding it to the code tool. I'm now ready to lay out a clear phased plan — automated steps first, manual review after — and present it to the user for approval rather than entering a formal plan mode, since this is really a guided migration workflow.

I now have everything I need. Here is the plan, built from your actual DDL rather than assumptions.

## What you're migrating

`BIGDATA`, 30 objects, one file (`db2_ddl/bigdata.sql`, 1,110 lines):

- **2 sequences** — `SEQ_AUDIT_BATCH`, `SEQ_INVOICE_NO`
- **11 tables** — `CUSTOMERS`, `INVOICES`, `INVOICE_LINES`, `PRODUCTS`, `PROMOTIONS`, `ORDERS`, `ORDER_ITEMS`, `INVENTORY`, `INVENTORY_TRANSACTIONS`, `CUSTOMER_AUDIT`, `CUSTOMER_SALES_SUMMARY`
- **3 functions** — `FN_INVOICE_TOTAL`, `FN_FORMAT_INVNO`, `FN_CUSTOMER_FULLNAME`
- **8 views** — including `V_CUSTOMER_360_ORDERS`, `V_ORDER_FULFILLMENT_STATUS`, `V_INVENTORY_RESTOCK_ALERT`
- **6 procedures** — `SP_ADD_CUSTOMER`, `SP_PLACE_ORDER`, `SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE`, `SP_REFRESH_CUSTOMER_SUMMARY`, `SP_RESTOCK_INVENTORY`, `SP_UPDATE_CUSTOMER_ADDRESS`

No triggers, and every routine is `LANGUAGE SQL` — no embedded C or Java to rewrite.

## Where the difficulty actually is

| Area | Count | Risk | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ORGANIZE BY COLUMN` + `USERSPACE1` tablespace | 11 | None | Snowflake micro-partitions automatically; these clauses are simply dropped |
| `PRIMARY KEY` / `FOREIGN KEY` via `ALTER TABLE` | 36 | **Medium** | Snowflake *accepts* but does **not enforce** FK, unique or check constraints. Your 15 FKs become documentation only |
| `IDENTITY` / `GENERATED ALWAYS` | 7 / 6 | Medium | Snowflake's `AUTOINCREMENT` doesn't guarantee gapless or reusable sequences the way DB2 does |
| Sequences + `NEXT VALUE FOR` | 2 | Low | Maps to `.NEXTVAL` |
| Views | 8 | Low–Medium | Join-heavy; mostly mechanical |
| Functions | 3 | Low–Medium | `FN_FORMAT_INVNO` does numeric formatting, a classic dialect divergence |
| **Procedures** — 2 cursors, 4 EXIT handlers, 2 CONTINUE handlers, 4 WHILE loops, 1 `GET DIAGNOSTICS` | 6 | **High** | DB2 SQL PL → Snowflake Scripting. Cursor-loop and condition-handler semantics differ; these need human review |

The six procedures are the real work. Everything else is largely mechanical.

## The plan

**Step 1 — Split the file.** All 30 objects are in one file. The importer splits on object boundaries, so I'll run the splitter first to tag each object, giving you 30 independently trackable units instead of one opaque blob.

**Step 2 — Register.** Import the split files so each object becomes a code unit with its own status, dependencies and history.

**Step 3 — Convert.** Run SnowConvert over all 30. Produces Snowflake SQL plus per-object EWIs (conversion warnings) and any out-of-scope constructs.

**Step 4 — Assess.** Generate the assessment report: what converted cleanly, what carries warnings, what needs judgment. My expectation is tables and sequences clean, views and functions mostly clean, and the procedures carrying the warnings.

**Step 5 — Review the procedures with you.** Walk the flagged conversions together, particularly the cursor loops and error handlers, and decide the right Snowflake equivalent for each.

Two things I want to be straight about before we start:

**The constraint gap is a real design decision, not a conversion bug.** Your schema leans on 15 enforced foreign keys. Snowflake won't enforce them. If `SP_PLACE_ORDER` relies on the database rejecting a bad `ORDER_ITEMS` row, that protection disappears and has to move into application logic or a validation step. We should decide deliberately.

**Steps 1–4 are automated; everything after is manual for DB2.** As established, DB2 is conversion-only here — no automated deploy, no equivalence testing against DB2, no orchestrated data migration. You'll get correct Snowflake SQL and a clear report, then deploy and move data yourself. I can help write and verify those steps, but the tooling won't drive them.

Shall I start with steps 1–4 and bring you the assessment?

So the arrange-then-merge pattern applies only to SqlServer, Redshift, Teradata, and Postgresql, while other languages copy source directly, and the code-already-split flag only works for that first group. This means Db2 has no arrange phase or code-unit registry — it's flat-file conversion only, which fits with the rest of the project.

So per-object tracking with trackable units and waves isn't available for Db2; conversion runs over the whole file, which means my earlier plan to split and register 30 units doesn't apply here. The right path is simpler: convert the files as-is and review the output, skipping the registry and per-object workflow, and I shouldn't bother with --code-already-split since it's only meant for the other four dialects and could mislead the project type. I'll proceed with the split-tagged source file since the split markers are just harmless SQL comments, then move on to actually running the conversion after checking progress and the convert skill.

Another DB2 limitation, and this one invalidates part of the plan I gave you. From the CLI's own documentation:

- *"SqlServer, Redshift, Teradata, and Postgresql: arranges source code, then merges processed output into `source/`"*
- *"**Other languages: copies source directly into `source/`**"*
- `--code-already-split` — *"SqlServer, Redshift, Teradata, and Postgresql **only**"*

**DB2 has no arrange phase and no code-unit registry.** That's why `query_registry` found nothing and `byType` was empty — it isn't a failure, it's the DB2 path working as designed. The splitting I did was wasted effort on my part; the tags are harmless SQL comments, but they bought us nothing.

The practical consequence for your plan: **there is no per-object tracking for DB2.** No 30 individually-tracked units, no waves, no per-object status, no object-by-object fix loop. Conversion runs over the file as a whole and emits Snowflake SQL plus a report. I described steps 1–2 as producing "30 independently trackable units" — that was wrong, and I should have verified dialect support before promising it rather than after.

Revised, and now grounded in what the tool actually does for DB2:

1. ~~Split~~ — not applicable

3. **Convert** `source/bigdata.sql` with SnowConvert → Snowflake SQL + EWI report
4. **Assess** the conversion output
5. **Review the six procedures with you**, driven by the EWI report rather than by object status

186...

189... | Return is a JSON object | `error: "no response"` |

195... dispatch the parent already intended to skip. Because a skip had nothing to
196... write, its `output_json: null` is the correct answer; it has no manifest and no

An `ok` return with one or more summary rows is complete only when every summary row has a non-empty `problem_description` and `recommended_fix`. This confirms it—all 56 Critical parse errors trace back to db2look's session-setup statements like setting NLS string units, current schema, and current path. These are just db2look scaffolding rather than actual business logic, and SnowConvert's DB2 grammar simply doesn't recognize that syntax.

There's also a subtler issue: the schema name "BIGDATA " has a trailing space baked in, a known db2look quirk. If left as-is, Snowflake would end up with a schema literally named with that trailing space, which would cause real downstream problems.

So the remediation path is clear: strip out the SET SYSIBM/CURRENT SCHEMA/CURRENT PATH lines, trim the trailing space from the schema name, and re-run the conversion—that should resolve the bulk of the critical errors.

I also need to correct something I said earlier. I claimed there were no critical EWIs based on the envelope summary, but looking more carefully, the envelope's "unique: 3" and severity breakdown of medium:1/low:2 only counts certain EWI codes and appears to exclude EWI-0001 (Critical) entirely—likely because it's tracked as a parse error rather than a standard EWI. The CSV actually shows 4 distinct EWI codes plus one FDM code, which doesn't match the envelope's tally. I need to flag this discrepancy plainly rather than let my earlier statement stand uncorrected.

Now I want to lay out the findings clearly: the correction, then the breakdown of issues by code—EWI-0035 for unsupported CHECK statements (11 occurrences, tied to dropped check constraints), FDM-0027 for removed clauses not applicable in Snowflake (22 occurrences, likely ENABLE QUERY OPTIMIZATION/ENFORCED), EWI-0120 for removed sequence options like MIN/MAX/CYCLE (2 occurrences), and EWI-0073 for items pending functional equivalence review (41 occurrences, covering parameter modes, DAYS, SIGNAL, condition declarations). I'll present this summary, make sure the correction is prominent, and then ask the user whether to proceed with the cleanup and reconversion.

Confirmed, and I need to correct something I told you.

## Correction

After conversion I said *"No critical or high-severity EWIs."* **That was wrong.** I took it from the JSON envelope, which reported `ewi.unique: 3` with only `medium: 1, low: 2`. The actual `Issues` CSV contains **132 issue rows including 56 Critical ones** — the envelope's EWI tally silently excludes parse errors. I should have checked the report before characterising the result, especially since the envelope was the only thing I'd looked at.

## What the 56 Critical issues actually are

All 56 are `SSC-EWI-0001 — Error parsing the source code`, and every one points at a `SET` statement:

```
UNRECOGNIZED TOKEN ON LINE '471' ... STARTING AT 'SET'. EXPECTED 'STATEMENT' GRAMMAR.
```

Line 471 is this:

```sql
SET SYSIBM.NLS_STRING_UNITS = 'SYSTEM';
```

These are **`db2look` scaffolding, not your code.** The dump repeats a session-settings preamble (`SET SYSIBM.NLS_STRING_UNITS`, `SET CURRENT SCHEMA`, `SET CURRENT PATH`) before every object. SnowConvert's DB2 grammar doesn't accept them, so each one throws a Critical parse error. None of your tables, views, functions or procedures caused a single one.

That's genuinely good news — but it also means the conversion ran with 56 statements unparsed, so the output can't be trusted until they're removed and it's re-run.

## The rest of the issues

| Code | Severity | Count | What it means |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SSC-EWI-0001` | Critical | 56 | `db2look` `SET` preamble — removable noise |
| `SSC-EWI-0073` | Medium | 41 | Pending functional-equivalence review: IN/OUT parameter modes (29), `SIGNAL` (2), condition declarations (2), `DAYS` date arithmetic (2) |
| `SSC-FDM-0027` | None | 22 | `ENFORCED` / `ENABLE QUERY OPTIMIZATION` clauses dropped — expected |
| `SSC-EWI-0035` | Low | 11 | **`CHECK STATEMENT NOT SUPPORTED`** — all 11 check constraints dropped |
| `SSC-EWI-0120` | Low | 2 | Sequence `MIN VALUE`/`MAX VALUE`/`CYCLE` options removed |

Two findings worth your attention beyond the parse errors:

**Your 11 check constraints are gone**, on top of the 15 unenforced foreign keys I flagged earlier. Rules like `DISCOUNT_PCT BETWEEN 0 AND 100` and `ACTIVE_FLAG IN ('Y','N')` are no longer enforced anywhere.

**`db2look` emitted your schema as `"BIGDATA "` — with a trailing space.** Taken literally that creates a Snowflake schema whose name ends in a space, which is valid but painful. This needs fixing before deploy.

## Also: the assessment stage can't run

Separately from all the above — `waves`, `object-exclusion` and `data-lineage` all require the registry DB2 never creates, and `anti-patterns` and `effort-estimate` are marked **(Not Available)** in this build. So there's no `multi_report.html` and no dependency waves for this project. SnowConvert's own `AssessmentReport.docx` is in `.scai/reports/SnowConvert/`, and the breakdown above is the substance the HTML report would have shown.

## What I propose

Clean the input and re-convert: strip the `SET SYSIBM.NLS_STRING_UNITS` / `SET CURRENT SCHEMA` / `SET CURRENT PATH` scaffolding lines, correct `"BIGDATA "` to `BIGDATA`, then re-run conversion with `--overwrite-working-directory`. I'd expect the 56 Criticals to go to zero, leaving the 41 equivalence reviews as the real work.

/* <sc-procedure>SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE</sc-procedure> */
CREATE PROCEDURE SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE (
  OUT P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT INTEGER,
  OUT P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  INTEGER
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_ON_HAND      INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_ALLOCATED    INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_REORDER_PT   INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_AVAIL        INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_AT_END       SMALLINT DEFAULT 0;--

  DECLARE C_SHORTAGE CURSOR FOR
    SELECT ON_HAND_QTY, ALLOCATED_QTY, REORDER_POINT
      FROM INVENTORY
     WHERE (ON_HAND_QTY - ALLOCATED_QTY) < REORDER_POINT;--

  DECLARE CONTINUE HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SET V_AT_END = 1;--

  SET P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT = 0;--
  SET P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  = 0;--

  OPEN C_SHORTAGE;--
  FETCH C_SHORTAGE INTO V_ON_HAND, V_ALLOCATED, V_REORDER_PT;--

  WHILE V_AT_END = 0 DO
    SET V_AVAIL = V_ON_HAND - V_ALLOCATED;--
    SET P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT = P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT + 1;--
    SET P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  = P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT + (V_REORDER_PT - V_AVAIL);--

    FETCH C_SHORTAGE INTO V_ON_HAND, V_ALLOCATED, V_REORDER_PT;--
  END WHILE;--

  CLOSE C_SHORTAGE;--
END;--;

/* <sc-procedure>SP_PLACE_ORDER</sc-procedure> */
CREATE PROCEDURE SP_PLACE_ORDER (
  IN  P_CUSTNO         CHAR(6),
  IN  P_ORDER_NO       CHAR(8),
  IN  P_PAYMENT_METHOD VARCHAR(20),
  IN  P_SUBTOTAL       DECIMAL(11,2),
  OUT P_ORDER_ID       INTEGER,
  OUT P_TOTAL_AMOUNT   DECIMAL(11,2)
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CUST_EXISTS INTEGER DEFAULT 0;--
  DECLARE V_TAX         DECIMAL(9,2) DEFAULT 0.00;--
  DECLARE V_FREIGHT     DECIMAL(9,2) DEFAULT 15.00;--
  DECLARE V_STATE       CHAR(2);--
  DECLARE CUST_MISSING  CONDITION FOR SQLSTATE '75002';--

  DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SIGNAL CUST_MISSING SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Customer does not exist in CUSTOMERS table';--

  SELECT STATE INTO V_STATE
    FROM CUSTOMERS
   WHERE CUSTNO = P_CUSTNO;--

  -- Apply 6% tax for TX, 7% for CA/NY
  IF V_STATE = 'TX' THEN
    SET V_TAX = ROUND(P_SUBTOTAL * 0.06, 2);--
  ELSEIF V_STATE IN ('CA', 'NY') THEN
    SET V_TAX = ROUND(P_SUBTOTAL * 0.07, 2);--
  ELSE
    SET V_TAX = 0.00;--
  END IF;--

  SET P_TOTAL_AMOUNT = P_SUBTOTAL + V_TAX + V_FREIGHT;--

  INSERT INTO ORDERS (

/* <sc-procedure>SP_REFRESH_CUSTOMER_SUMMARY</sc-procedure> */
CREATE PROCEDURE SP_REFRESH_CUSTOMER_SUMMARY (OUT P_ROWS INTEGER)
  LANGUAGE SQL
  MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CUSTNO  CHAR(6);--
  DECLARE V_COUNT   INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_TOTAL   DECIMAL(11,2);--
  DECLARE V_LAST    DATE;--
  DECLARE V_AT_END  SMALLINT DEFAULT 0;--

  DECLARE C1 CURSOR FOR
    SELECT INVCUST, COUNT(*), SUM(INVTOTAL), MAX(INVDATE)
      FROM INVOICES
     GROUP BY INVCUST
     ORDER BY INVCUST;--

  DECLARE CONTINUE HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SET V_AT_END = 1;--

  SET P_ROWS = 0;--

  DELETE FROM CUSTOMER_SALES_SUMMARY;--

  OPEN C1;--
  FETCH C1 INTO V_CUSTNO, V_COUNT, V_TOTAL, V_LAST;--

  WHILE V_AT_END = 0 DO
    INSERT INTO CUSTOMER_SALES_SUMMARY
           (CUSTNO, INVOICE_COUNT, TOTAL_SALES, LAST_INVOICE_DATE, REFRESHED_TS)
    VALUES (V_CUSTNO, V_COUNT, V_TOTAL, V_LAST, CURRENT TIMESTAMP);--

    SET P_ROWS = P_ROWS + 1;--
    FETCH C1 INTO V_CUSTNO, V_COUNT, V_TOTAL, V_LAST;--
  END WHILE;--

  CLOSE C1;--
END;--;

/* <sc-procedure>SP_RESTOCK_INVENTORY</sc-procedure> */
CREATE PROCEDURE SP_RESTOCK_INVENTORY (
  IN  P_WAREHOUSE_ID   CHAR(4),
  IN  P_PRODUCT_ID     INTEGER,
  IN  P_RESTOCK_QTY    INTEGER,
  IN  P_OPERATOR_ID    VARCHAR(20),
  IN  P_PO_NUMBER      VARCHAR(30),
  OUT P_NEW_ON_HAND    INTEGER
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CURRENT_QTY INTEGER;--
  DECLARE INV_NOT_FOUND CONDITION FOR SQLSTATE '75003';--

  DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SIGNAL INV_NOT_FOUND SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Warehouse product inventory record not found';--

  SELECT ON_HAND_QTY INTO V_CURRENT_QTY
    FROM INVENTORY
   WHERE WAREHOUSE_ID = P_WAREHOUSE_ID
     AND PRODUCT_ID = P_PRODUCT_ID;--

  SET P_NEW_ON_HAND = V_CURRENT_QTY + P_RESTOCK_QTY;--

  UPDATE INVENTORY
     SET ON_HAND_QTY = P_NEW_ON_HAND,
         LAST_RESTOCK_DATE = CURRENT DATE,
         LAST_AUDIT_TS = CURRENT TIMESTAMP
   WHERE WAREHOUSE_ID = P_WAREHOUSE_ID
     AND PRODUCT_ID = P_PRODUCT_ID;--

  INSERT INTO INVENTORY_TRANSACTIONS (
    PRODUCT_ID,
    WAREHOUSE_ID,
    TXN_TYPE,
    QUANTITY,
    REFERENCE_NO,
    OPERATOR_ID,
    NOTES
  ) VALUES (
    P_PRODUCT_ID,
    P_WAREHOUSE_ID,
    'RECEIPT',
    P_RESTOCK_QTY,
    P_PO_NUMBER,
    P_OPERATOR_ID,
    'Restock replenishment processed successfully'
  );--

END;--;

  IN  P_CUSTNO  CHAR(6),

  IN  P_STATE   CHAR(2),
  IN  P_ZIP     VARCHAR(10),
  OUT P_ROWS    INTEGER)
  LANGUAGE SQL
  MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN

     SET ADDR    = P_ADDR,
         CITY    = P_CITY,
         STATE   = P_STATE,
         ZIPCODE = P_ZIP
   WHERE CUSTNO = P_CUSTNO;--

    VALUES (P_CUSTNO, 'U', 'Address changed');--
  END IF;--

  SET P_ROWS = V_ROWS;--
END;--;

/* <sc-procedure>SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE</sc-procedure> */
CREATE PROCEDURE SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE (
  OUT P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT INTEGER,
  OUT P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  INTEGER
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_ON_HAND      INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_ALLOCATED    INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_REORDER_PT   INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_AVAIL        INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_AT_END       SMALLINT DEFAULT 0;--

  DECLARE C_SHORTAGE CURSOR FOR
    SELECT ON_HAND_QTY, ALLOCATED_QTY, REORDER_POINT
      FROM INVENTORY
     WHERE (ON_HAND_QTY - ALLOCATED_QTY) < REORDER_POINT;--

  DECLARE CONTINUE HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SET V_AT_END = 1;--

  SET P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT = 0;--
  SET P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  = 0;--

  OPEN C_SHORTAGE;--
  FETCH C_SHORTAGE INTO V_ON_HAND, V_ALLOCATED, V_REORDER_PT;--

  WHILE V_AT_END = 0 DO
    SET V_AVAIL = V_ON_HAND - V_ALLOCATED;--
    SET P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT = P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT + 1;--
    SET P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  = P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT + (V_REORDER_PT - V_AVAIL);--

    FETCH C_SHORTAGE INTO V_ON_HAND, V_ALLOCATED, V_REORDER_PT;--
  END WHILE;--

  CLOSE C_SHORTAGE;--
END;--;

/* <sc-procedure>SP_PLACE_ORDER</sc-procedure> */
CREATE PROCEDURE SP_PLACE_ORDER (
  IN  P_CUSTNO         CHAR(6),
  IN  P_ORDER_NO       CHAR(8),
  IN  P_PAYMENT_METHOD VARCHAR(20),
  IN  P_SUBTOTAL       DECIMAL(11,2),
  OUT P_ORDER_ID       INTEGER,
  OUT P_TOTAL_AMOUNT   DECIMAL(11,2)
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CUST_EXISTS INTEGER DEFAULT 0;--
  DECLARE V_TAX         DECIMAL(9,2) DEFAULT 0.00;--
  DECLARE V_FREIGHT     DECIMAL(9,2) DEFAULT 15.00;--
  DECLARE V_STATE       CHAR(2);--
  DECLARE CUST_MISSING  CONDITION FOR SQLSTATE '75002';--

  DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SIGNAL CUST_MISSING SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Customer does not exist in CUSTOMERS table';--

  SELECT STATE INTO V_STATE
    FROM CUSTOMERS
   WHERE CUSTNO = P_CUSTNO;--

  -- Apply 6% tax for TX, 7% for CA/NY
  IF V_STATE = 'TX' THEN
    SET V_TAX = ROUND(P_SUBTOTAL * 0.06, 2);--
  ELSEIF V_STATE IN ('CA', 'NY') THEN
    SET V_TAX = ROUND(P_SUBTOTAL * 0.07, 2);--
  ELSE
    SET V_TAX = 0.00;--
  END IF;--

  SET P_TOTAL_AMOUNT = P_SUBTOTAL + V_TAX + V_FREIGHT;--

  INSERT INTO ORDERS (
    ORDER_NO,
    CUSTNO,
    ORDER_DATE,
    REQUIRED_DATE,
    STATUS,
    SUBTOTAL,
    TAX_AMOUNT,
    FREIGHT_CHARGE,
    TOTAL_AMOUNT,
    PAYMENT_METHOD,
    PAYMENT_STATUS
  ) VALUES (
    P_ORDER_NO,
    P_CUSTNO,
    CURRENT DATE,
    CURRENT DATE + 7 DAYS,
    'PENDING',
    P_SUBTOTAL,
    V_TAX,
    V_FREIGHT,
    P_TOTAL_AMOUNT,
    P_PAYMENT_METHOD,
    'AUTHORIZED'
  );--

  SELECT ORDER_ID INTO P_ORDER_ID
    FROM ORDERS
   WHERE ORDER_NO = P_ORDER_NO;--

END;--
;

CREATE PROCEDURE SP_REFRESH_CUSTOMER_SUMMARY (OUT P_ROWS INTEGER)
  LANGUAGE SQL
  MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CUSTNO  CHAR(6);--
  DECLARE V_COUNT   INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_TOTAL   DECIMAL(11,2);--
  DECLARE V_LAST    DATE;--
  DECLARE V_AT_END  SMALLINT DEFAULT 0;--

  DECLARE C1 CURSOR FOR
    SELECT INVCUST, COUNT(*), SUM(INVTOTAL), MAX(INVDATE)
      FROM INVOICES
     GROUP BY INVCUST
     ORDER BY INVCUST;--

  DECLARE CONTINUE HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SET V_AT_END = 1;--

  SET P_ROWS = 0;--

  DELETE FROM CUSTOMER_SALES_SUMMARY;--

  OPEN C1;--
  FETCH C1 INTO V_CUSTNO, V_COUNT, V_TOTAL, V_LAST;--

    SET P_ROWS = P_ROWS + 1;--
    FETCH C1 INTO V_CUSTNO, V_COUNT, V_TOTAL, V_LAST;--
  END WHILE;--

/* <sc-procedure>SP_RESTOCK_INVENTORY</sc-procedure> */
CREATE PROCEDURE SP_RESTOCK_INVENTORY (
  IN  P_WAREHOUSE_ID   CHAR(4),
  IN  P_PRODUCT_ID     INTEGER,
  IN  P_RESTOCK_QTY    INTEGER,
  IN  P_OPERATOR_ID    VARCHAR(20),
  IN  P_PO_NUMBER      VARCHAR(30),
  OUT P_NEW_ON_HAND    INTEGER
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CURRENT_QTY INTEGER;--
  DECLARE INV_NOT_FOUND CONDITION FOR SQLSTATE '75003';--

  DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SIGNAL INV_NOT_FOUND SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Warehouse product inventory record not found';--

  SELECT ON_HAND_QTY INTO V_CURRENT_QTY
    FROM INVENTORY
   WHERE WAREHOUSE_ID = P_WAREHOUSE_ID
     AND PRODUCT_ID = P_PRODUCT_ID;--

  SET P_NEW_ON_HAND = V_CURRENT_QTY + P_RESTOCK_QTY;--

  UPDATE INVENTORY
     SET ON_HAND_QTY = P_NEW_ON_HAND,
         LAST_RESTOCK_DATE = CURRENT DATE,
         LAST_AUDIT_TS = CURRENT TIMESTAMP
   WHERE WAREHOUSE_ID = P_WAREHOUSE_ID
     AND PRODUCT_ID = P_PRODUCT_ID;--

  INSERT INTO INVENTORY_TRANSACTIONS (
    PRODUCT_ID,
    WAREHOUSE_ID,
    TXN_TYPE,
    QUANTITY,
    REFERENCE_NO,
    OPERATOR_ID,
    NOTES
  ) VALUES (
    P_PRODUCT_ID,
    P_WAREHOUSE_ID,
    'RECEIPT',
    P_RESTOCK_QTY,
    P_PO_NUMBER,
    P_OPERATOR_ID,
    'Restock replenishment processed successfully'
  );--

/* <sc-view>V_MONTHLY_SALES</sc-view> */
CREATE VIEW V_MONTHLY_SALES AS

/* <sc-view>V_PRODUCT_SALES</sc-view> */
CREATE VIEW V_PRODUCT_SALES AS
SELECT P.SKU,
       P.PRODUCT_NAME,
       P.CATEGORY,
       COALESCE(SUM(L.QUANTITY), 0) AS UNITS_SOLD,
       COALESCE(SUM(L.LINE_TOTAL), 0) AS REVENUE

     LEFT OUTER JOIN INVOICE_LINES L
     ON L.PRODUCT_ID = P.PRODUCT_ID

/* <sc-view>V_PROMO_USAGE</sc-view> */
CREATE VIEW V_PROMO_USAGE AS
SELECT R.PROMO_CODE,
       R.PROMO_NAME,
       R.DISCOUNT_PCT,

/* <sc-view>V_ORDER_FULFILLMENT_STATUS</sc-view> */
CREATE VIEW V_ORDER_FULFILLMENT_STATUS AS
SELECT O.ORDER_ID,
       O.ORDER_NO,
       O.CUSTNO,
       RTRIM(C.FNAME) || ' ' || RTRIM(C.LNAME) AS CUSTOMER_NAME,
       C.STATE,
       O.ORDER_DATE,
       O.REQUIRED_DATE,
       O.SHIPPED_DATE,
       CASE
         WHEN O.SHIPPED_DATE IS NOT NULL THEN (DAYS(O.SHIPPED_DATE) - DAYS(O.ORDER_DATE))
         ELSE NULL
       END AS FULFILLMENT_DAYS,
       O.STATUS,
       O.TOTAL_AMOUNT,
       COUNT(OI.ITEM_ID) AS ITEM_COUNT,
       COALESCE(SUM(OI.QUANTITY), 0) AS TOTAL_UNITS
FROM ORDERS O
     INNER JOIN CUSTOMERS C ON C.CUSTNO = O.CUSTNO

/* <sc-view>V_INVENTORY_RESTOCK_ALERT</sc-view> */
CREATE VIEW V_INVENTORY_RESTOCK_ALERT AS
SELECT I.WAREHOUSE_ID,
       P.PRODUCT_ID,
       P.SKU,
       P.PRODUCT_NAME,
       I.ON_HAND_QTY,
       I.ALLOCATED_QTY,
       (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) AS AVAILABLE_QTY,
       I.REORDER_POINT,
       I.REORDER_QTY,
       I.SAFETY_STOCK,
       I.BIN_LOCATION,
       CASE
         WHEN (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) <= I.SAFETY_STOCK THEN 'CRITICAL'
         WHEN (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) <= I.REORDER_POINT THEN 'REORDER_NOW'
         ELSE 'HEALTHY'
       END AS INVENTORY_STATUS
FROM INVENTORY I
     INNER JOIN PRODUCTS P ON P.PRODUCT_ID = I.PRODUCT_ID
WHERE (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) <= I.REORDER_POINT;

/* <sc-procedure>SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE</sc-procedure> */
CREATE PROCEDURE SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE (
  OUT P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT INTEGER,
  OUT P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  INTEGER
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_ON_HAND      INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_ALLOCATED    INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_REORDER_PT   INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_AVAIL        INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_AT_END       SMALLINT DEFAULT 0;--

  DECLARE C_SHORTAGE CURSOR FOR
    SELECT ON_HAND_QTY, ALLOCATED_QTY, REORDER_POINT
      FROM INVENTORY
     WHERE (ON_HAND_QTY - ALLOCATED_QTY) < REORDER_POINT;--

  DECLARE CONTINUE HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SET V_AT_END = 1;--

  SET P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT = 0;--
  SET P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  = 0;--

  OPEN C_SHORTAGE;--
  FETCH C_SHORTAGE INTO V_ON_HAND, V_ALLOCATED, V_REORDER_PT;--

  WHILE V_AT_END = 0 DO
    SET V_AVAIL = V_ON_HAND - V_ALLOCATED;--
    SET P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT = P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT + 1;--
    SET P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  = P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT + (V_REORDER_PT - V_AVAIL);--

    FETCH C_SHORTAGE INTO V_ON_HAND, V_ALLOCATED, V_REORDER_PT;--
  END WHILE;--

  CLOSE C_SHORTAGE;--
END;--;

/* <sc-procedure>SP_PLACE_ORDER</sc-procedure> */
CREATE PROCEDURE SP_PLACE_ORDER (
  IN  P_CUSTNO         CHAR(6),
  IN  P_ORDER_NO       CHAR(8),
  IN  P_PAYMENT_METHOD VARCHAR(20),
  IN  P_SUBTOTAL       DECIMAL(11,2),
  OUT P_ORDER_ID       INTEGER,
  OUT P_TOTAL_AMOUNT   DECIMAL(11,2)
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CUST_EXISTS INTEGER DEFAULT 0;--
  DECLARE V_TAX         DECIMAL(9,2) DEFAULT 0.00;--
  DECLARE V_FREIGHT     DECIMAL(9,2) DEFAULT 15.00;--
  DECLARE V_STATE       CHAR(2);--
  DECLARE CUST_MISSING  CONDITION FOR SQLSTATE '75002';--

  DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SIGNAL CUST_MISSING SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Customer does not exist in CUSTOMERS table';--

  SELECT STATE INTO V_STATE
    FROM CUSTOMERS
   WHERE CUSTNO = P_CUSTNO;--

  -- Apply 6% tax for TX, 7% for CA/NY
  IF V_STATE = 'TX' THEN
    SET V_TAX = ROUND(P_SUBTOTAL * 0.06, 2);--
  ELSEIF V_STATE IN ('CA', 'NY') THEN
    SET V_TAX = ROUND(P_SUBTOTAL * 0.07, 2);--
  ELSE
    SET V_TAX = 0.00;--
  END IF;--

  SET P_TOTAL_AMOUNT = P_SUBTOTAL + V_TAX + V_FREIGHT;--

  INSERT INTO ORDERS (
    ORDER_NO,
    CUSTNO,
    ORDER_DATE,
    REQUIRED_DATE,
    STATUS,
    SUBTOTAL,
    TAX_AMOUNT,
    FREIGHT_CHARGE,
    TOTAL_AMOUNT,
    PAYMENT_METHOD,
    PAYMENT_STATUS
  ) VALUES (
    P_ORDER_NO,
    P_CUSTNO,
    CURRENT DATE,
    CURRENT DATE + 7 DAYS,
    'PENDING',
    P_SUBTOTAL,
    V_TAX,
    V_FREIGHT,
    P_TOTAL_AMOUNT,
    P_PAYMENT_METHOD,
    'AUTHORIZED'
  );--

  SELECT ORDER_ID INTO P_ORDER_ID
    FROM ORDERS
   WHERE ORDER_NO = P_ORDER_NO;--

END;--
;

/* <sc-procedure>SP_RESTOCK_INVENTORY</sc-procedure> */
CREATE PROCEDURE SP_RESTOCK_INVENTORY (
  IN  P_WAREHOUSE_ID   CHAR(4),
  IN  P_PRODUCT_ID     INTEGER,
  IN  P_RESTOCK_QTY    INTEGER,
  IN  P_OPERATOR_ID    VARCHAR(20),
  IN  P_PO_NUMBER      VARCHAR(30),
  OUT P_NEW_ON_HAND    INTEGER
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CURRENT_QTY INTEGER;--
  DECLARE INV_NOT_FOUND CONDITION FOR SQLSTATE '75003';--

  DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SIGNAL INV_NOT_FOUND SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Warehouse product inventory record not found';--

  SELECT ON_HAND_QTY INTO V_CURRENT_QTY
    FROM INVENTORY
   WHERE WAREHOUSE_ID = P_WAREHOUSE_ID
     AND PRODUCT_ID = P_PRODUCT_ID;--

  SET P_NEW_ON_HAND = V_CURRENT_QTY + P_RESTOCK_QTY;--

  UPDATE INVENTORY
     SET ON_HAND_QTY = P_NEW_ON_HAND,
         LAST_RESTOCK_DATE = CURRENT DATE,
         LAST_AUDIT_TS = CURRENT TIMESTAMP
   WHERE WAREHOUSE_ID = P_WAREHOUSE_ID
     AND PRODUCT_ID = P_PRODUCT_ID;--

  INSERT INTO INVENTORY_TRANSACTIONS (
    PRODUCT_ID,
    WAREHOUSE_ID,
    TXN_TYPE,
    QUANTITY,
    REFERENCE_NO,
    OPERATOR_ID,
    NOTES

    P_WAREHOUSE_ID,
    'RECEIPT',
    P_RESTOCK_QTY,
    P_PO_NUMBER,
    P_OPERATOR_ID,
    'Restock replenishment processed successfully'

/* <sc-view>V_INVENTORY_RESTOCK_ALERT</sc-view> */
CREATE VIEW V_INVENTORY_RESTOCK_ALERT AS
SELECT I.WAREHOUSE_ID,
       P.PRODUCT_ID,
       P.SKU,
       P.PRODUCT_NAME,
       I.ON_HAND_QTY,
       I.ALLOCATED_QTY,
       (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) AS AVAILABLE_QTY,
       I.REORDER_POINT,
       I.REORDER_QTY,
       I.SAFETY_STOCK,
       I.BIN_LOCATION,
       CASE
         WHEN (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) <= I.SAFETY_STOCK THEN 'CRITICAL'
         WHEN (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) <= I.REORDER_POINT THEN 'REORDER_NOW'
         ELSE 'HEALTHY'
       END AS INVENTORY_STATUS
FROM INVENTORY I
     INNER JOIN PRODUCTS P ON P.PRODUCT_ID = I.PRODUCT_ID
WHERE (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) <= I.REORDER_POINT;

/* <sc-procedure>SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE</sc-procedure> */
CREATE PROCEDURE SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE (
  OUT P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT INTEGER,
  OUT P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  INTEGER
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_ON_HAND      INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_ALLOCATED    INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_REORDER_PT   INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_AVAIL        INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_AT_END       SMALLINT DEFAULT 0;--

  DECLARE C_SHORTAGE CURSOR FOR
    SELECT ON_HAND_QTY, ALLOCATED_QTY, REORDER_POINT
      FROM INVENTORY
     WHERE (ON_HAND_QTY - ALLOCATED_QTY) < REORDER_POINT;--

  DECLARE CONTINUE HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SET V_AT_END = 1;--

  SET P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT = 0;--
  SET P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  = 0;--

  OPEN C_SHORTAGE;--
  FETCH C_SHORTAGE INTO V_ON_HAND, V_ALLOCATED, V_REORDER_PT;--

  WHILE V_AT_END = 0 DO

/* <sc-procedure>SP_PLACE_ORDER</sc-procedure> */
CREATE PROCEDURE SP_PLACE_ORDER (
  IN  P_CUSTNO         CHAR(6),
  IN  P_ORDER_NO       CHAR(8),
  IN  P_PAYMENT_METHOD VARCHAR(20),
  IN  P_SUBTOTAL       DECIMAL(11,2),
  OUT P_ORDER_ID       INTEGER,
  OUT P_TOTAL_AMOUNT   DECIMAL(11,2)
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CUST_EXISTS INTEGER DEFAULT 0;--
  DECLARE V_TAX         DECIMAL(9,2) DEFAULT 0.00;--
  DECLARE V_FREIGHT     DECIMAL(9,2) DEFAULT 15.00;--
  DECLARE V_STATE       CHAR(2);--
  DECLARE CUST_MISSING  CONDITION FOR SQLSTATE '75002';--

  DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SIGNAL CUST_MISSING SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Customer does not exist in CUSTOMERS table';--

  SELECT STATE INTO V_STATE
    FROM CUSTOMERS
   WHERE CUSTNO = P_CUSTNO;--

  -- Apply 6% tax for TX, 7% for CA/NY
  IF V_STATE = 'TX' THEN
    SET V_TAX = ROUND(P_SUBTOTAL * 0.06, 2);--
  ELSEIF V_STATE IN ('CA', 'NY') THEN
    SET V_TAX = ROUND(P_SUBTOTAL * 0.07, 2);--
  ELSE
    SET V_TAX = 0.00;--
  END IF;--

  SET P_TOTAL_AMOUNT = P_SUBTOTAL + V_TAX + V_FREIGHT;--

  INSERT INTO ORDERS (
    ORDER_NO,
    CUSTNO,
    ORDER_DATE,
    REQUIRED_DATE,
    STATUS,
    SUBTOTAL,
    TAX_AMOUNT,
    FREIGHT_CHARGE,
    TOTAL_AMOUNT,
    PAYMENT_METHOD,
    PAYMENT_STATUS
  ) VALUES (
    P_ORDER_NO,
    P_CUSTNO,
    CURRENT DATE,
    CURRENT DATE + 7 DAYS,
    'PENDING',
    P_SUBTOTAL,
    V_TAX,
    V_FREIGHT,
    P_TOTAL_AMOUNT,
    P_PAYMENT_METHOD,
    'AUTHORIZED'
  );--

  SELECT ORDER_ID INTO P_ORDER_ID
    FROM ORDERS
   WHERE ORDER_NO = P_ORDER_NO;--

END;--
;

CREATE PROCEDURE SP_REFRESH_CUSTOMER_SUMMARY (OUT P_ROWS INTEGER)
  LANGUAGE SQL
  MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CUSTNO  CHAR(6);--

  DECLARE V_TOTAL   DECIMAL(11,2);--

    SET V_AT_END = 1;--

  SET P_ROWS = 0;--

  DELETE FROM CUSTOMER_SALES_SUMMARY;--

  OPEN C1;--
  FETCH C1 INTO V_CUSTNO, V_COUNT, V_TOTAL, V_LAST;--

           (CUSTNO, INVOICE_COUNT, TOTAL_SALES, LAST_INVOICE_DATE, REFRESHED_TS)
    VALUES (V_CUSTNO, V_COUNT, V_TOTAL, V_LAST, CURRENT TIMESTAMP);--

    SET P_ROWS = P_ROWS + 1;--
    FETCH C1 INTO V_CUSTNO, V_COUNT, V_TOTAL, V_LAST;--
  END WHILE;--

  CLOSE C1;--

/* <sc-procedure>SP_RESTOCK_INVENTORY</sc-procedure> */
CREATE PROCEDURE SP_RESTOCK_INVENTORY (
  IN  P_WAREHOUSE_ID   CHAR(4),
  IN  P_PRODUCT_ID     INTEGER,
  IN  P_RESTOCK_QTY    INTEGER,
  IN  P_OPERATOR_ID    VARCHAR(20),
  IN  P_PO_NUMBER      VARCHAR(30),
  OUT P_NEW_ON_HAND    INTEGER
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CURRENT_QTY INTEGER;--
  DECLARE INV_NOT_FOUND CONDITION FOR SQLSTATE '75003';--

  DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SIGNAL INV_NOT_FOUND SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Warehouse product inventory record not found';--

  SELECT ON_HAND_QTY INTO V_CURRENT_QTY
    FROM INVENTORY
   WHERE WAREHOUSE_ID = P_WAREHOUSE_ID
     AND PRODUCT_ID = P_PRODUCT_ID;--

  SET P_NEW_ON_HAND = V_CURRENT_QTY + P_RESTOCK_QTY;--

  UPDATE INVENTORY
     SET ON_HAND_QTY = P_NEW_ON_HAND,
         LAST_RESTOCK_DATE = CURRENT DATE,
         LAST_AUDIT_TS = CURRENT TIMESTAMP
   WHERE WAREHOUSE_ID = P_WAREHOUSE_ID
     AND PRODUCT_ID = P_PRODUCT_ID;--

  INSERT INTO INVENTORY_TRANSACTIONS (
    PRODUCT_ID,
    WAREHOUSE_ID,
    TXN_TYPE,
    QUANTITY,
    REFERENCE_NO,
    OPERATOR_ID,
    NOTES
  ) VALUES (
    P_PRODUCT_ID,
    P_WAREHOUSE_ID,
    'RECEIPT',
    P_RESTOCK_QTY,
    P_PO_NUMBER,
    P_OPERATOR_ID,
    'Restock replenishment processed successfully'
  );--

/* <sc-procedure>SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE</sc-procedure> */
CREATE PROCEDURE SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE (
  OUT P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT INTEGER,
  OUT P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  INTEGER
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_ON_HAND      INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_ALLOCATED    INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_REORDER_PT   INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_AVAIL        INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_AT_END       SMALLINT DEFAULT 0;--

  DECLARE C_SHORTAGE CURSOR FOR
    SELECT ON_HAND_QTY, ALLOCATED_QTY, REORDER_POINT
      FROM INVENTORY
     WHERE (ON_HAND_QTY - ALLOCATED_QTY) < REORDER_POINT;--

  DECLARE CONTINUE HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SET V_AT_END = 1;--

  SET P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT = 0;--
  SET P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  = 0;--

  OPEN C_SHORTAGE;--
  FETCH C_SHORTAGE INTO V_ON_HAND, V_ALLOCATED, V_REORDER_PT;--

  WHILE V_AT_END = 0 DO
    SET V_AVAIL = V_ON_HAND - V_ALLOCATED;--
    SET P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT = P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT + 1;--
    SET P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  = P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT + (V_REORDER_PT - V_AVAIL);--

    FETCH C_SHORTAGE INTO V_ON_HAND, V_ALLOCATED, V_REORDER_PT;--
  END WHILE;--

  CLOSE C_SHORTAGE;--
END;--;

/* <sc-procedure>SP_PLACE_ORDER</sc-procedure> */
CREATE PROCEDURE SP_PLACE_ORDER (
  IN  P_CUSTNO         CHAR(6),
  IN  P_ORDER_NO       CHAR(8),
  IN  P_PAYMENT_METHOD VARCHAR(20),
  IN  P_SUBTOTAL       DECIMAL(11,2),
  OUT P_ORDER_ID       INTEGER,
  OUT P_TOTAL_AMOUNT   DECIMAL(11,2)
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CUST_EXISTS INTEGER DEFAULT 0;--
  DECLARE V_TAX         DECIMAL(9,2) DEFAULT 0.00;--
  DECLARE V_FREIGHT     DECIMAL(9,2) DEFAULT 15.00;--
  DECLARE V_STATE       CHAR(2);--
  DECLARE CUST_MISSING  CONDITION FOR SQLSTATE '75002';--

  DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SIGNAL CUST_MISSING SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Customer does not exist in CUSTOMERS table';--

  SELECT STATE INTO V_STATE
    FROM CUSTOMERS
   WHERE CUSTNO = P_CUSTNO;--

  -- Apply 6% tax for TX, 7% for CA/NY
  IF V_STATE = 'TX' THEN
    SET V_TAX = ROUND(P_SUBTOTAL * 0.06, 2);--
  ELSEIF V_STATE IN ('CA', 'NY') THEN
    SET V_TAX = ROUND(P_SUBTOTAL * 0.07, 2);--
  ELSE
    SET V_TAX = 0.00;--
  END IF;--

  SET P_TOTAL_AMOUNT = P_SUBTOTAL + V_TAX + V_FREIGHT;--

  INSERT INTO ORDERS (
    ORDER_NO,
    CUSTNO,
    ORDER_DATE,
    REQUIRED_DATE,
    STATUS,
    SUBTOTAL,
    TAX_AMOUNT,
    FREIGHT_CHARGE,
    TOTAL_AMOUNT,
    PAYMENT_METHOD,
    PAYMENT_STATUS
  ) VALUES (
    P_ORDER_NO,
    P_CUSTNO,
    CURRENT DATE,
    CURRENT DATE + 7 DAYS,
    'PENDING',
    P_SUBTOTAL,
    V_TAX,
    V_FREIGHT,
    P_TOTAL_AMOUNT,
    P_PAYMENT_METHOD,
    'AUTHORIZED'
  );--

  SELECT ORDER_ID INTO P_ORDER_ID
    FROM ORDERS
   WHERE ORDER_NO = P_ORDER_NO;--

END;--
;

  DECLARE V_COUNT   INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_TOTAL   DECIMAL(11,2);--

  SET P_ROWS = 0;--

    FETCH C1 INTO V_CUSTNO, V_COUNT, V_TOTAL, V_LAST;--

CREATE PROCEDURE SP_RESTOCK_INVENTORY (

  IN  P_RESTOCK_QTY    INTEGER,
  IN  P_OPERATOR_ID    VARCHAR(20),

)
LANGUAGE SQL

BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CURRENT_QTY INTEGER;--
  DECLARE INV_NOT_FOUND CONDITION FOR SQLSTATE '75003';--

  DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SIGNAL INV_NOT_FOUND SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Warehouse product inventory record not found';--

  SELECT ON_HAND_QTY INTO V_CURRENT_QTY
    FROM INVENTORY
   WHERE WAREHOUSE_ID = P_WAREHOUSE_ID
     AND PRODUCT_ID = P_PRODUCT_ID;--

  SET P_NEW_ON_HAND = V_CURRENT_QTY + P_RESTOCK_QTY;--

  UPDATE INVENTORY
     SET ON_HAND_QTY = P_NEW_ON_HAND,
         LAST_RESTOCK_DATE = CURRENT DATE,
         LAST_AUDIT_TS = CURRENT TIMESTAMP
   WHERE WAREHOUSE_ID = P_WAREHOUSE_ID
     AND PRODUCT_ID = P_PRODUCT_ID;--

  INSERT INTO INVENTORY_TRANSACTIONS (
    PRODUCT_ID,
    WAREHOUSE_ID,
    TXN_TYPE,
    QUANTITY,
    REFERENCE_NO,
    OPERATOR_ID,
    NOTES
  ) VALUES (
    P_PRODUCT_ID,
    P_WAREHOUSE_ID,
    'RECEIPT',
    P_RESTOCK_QTY,
    P_PO_NUMBER,
    P_OPERATOR_ID,

  );--

BEGIN
  DECLARE V_ON_HAND      INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_ALLOCATED    INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_REORDER_PT   INTEGER;--

  DECLARE V_AT_END       SMALLINT DEFAULT 0;--

    SELECT ON_HAND_QTY, ALLOCATED_QTY, REORDER_POINT

    SET V_AT_END = 1;--

  OPEN C_SHORTAGE;--
  FETCH C_SHORTAGE INTO V_ON_HAND, V_ALLOCATED, V_REORDER_PT;--

  WHILE V_AT_END = 0 DO
    SET V_AVAIL = V_ON_HAND - V_ALLOCATED;--
    SET P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT = P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT + 1;--
    SET P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  = P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT + (V_REORDER_PT - V_AVAIL);--

    FETCH C_SHORTAGE INTO V_ON_HAND, V_ALLOCATED, V_REORDER_PT;--

CREATE VIEW V_CUSTOMER_INVOICES AS
SELECT C.CUSTNO,
       RTRIM(C.FNAME) || ' ' || RTRIM(C.LNAME) AS CUSTOMER_NAME,
       C.STATE,
       I.INVNO,
       I.INVDATE,
       I.INVTOTAL,
       I.INVPROM
FROM CUSTOMERS C
     INNER JOIN INVOICES I
     ON I.INVCUST = C.CUSTNO;


CREATE VIEW V_INVOICE_DETAIL AS
SELECT I.INVNO,
       I.INVDATE,
       I.INVCUST,
       L.LINE_NO,
       P.SKU,
       P.PRODUCT_NAME,
       L.QUANTITY,
       L.UNIT_PRICE,
       L.LINE_TOTAL
FROM INVOICES I
     INNER JOIN INVOICE_LINES L ON L.INVNO = I.INVNO
     INNER JOIN PRODUCTS P ON P.PRODUCT_ID = L.PRODUCT_ID;


CREATE VIEW V_MONTHLY_SALES AS
SELECT YEAR(INVDATE) AS SALES_YEAR,
       MONTH(INVDATE) AS SALES_MONTH,
       COUNT(*) AS INVOICE_COUNT,
       SUM(INVTOTAL) AS TOTAL_SALES,
       AVG(INVTOTAL) AS AVG_INVOICE
FROM INVOICES
GROUP BY YEAR(INVDATE), MONTH(INVDATE);


CREATE VIEW V_PRODUCT_SALES AS
SELECT P.SKU,
       P.PRODUCT_NAME,
       P.CATEGORY,
       COALESCE(SUM(L.QUANTITY), 0) AS UNITS_SOLD,
       COALESCE(SUM(L.LINE_TOTAL), 0) AS REVENUE
FROM PRODUCTS P
     LEFT OUTER JOIN INVOICE_LINES L
     ON L.PRODUCT_ID = P.PRODUCT_ID
GROUP BY P.SKU, P.PRODUCT_NAME, P.CATEGORY;


CREATE VIEW V_PROMO_USAGE AS
SELECT R.PROMO_CODE,
       R.PROMO_NAME,
       R.DISCOUNT_PCT,
       COUNT(I.INVNO) AS INVOICES_USED,
       COALESCE(SUM(I.INVTOTAL), 0) AS SALES_WITH_PROMO
FROM PROMOTIONS R
     LEFT OUTER JOIN INVOICES I
     ON I.INVPROM = R.PROMO_CODE
GROUP BY R.PROMO_CODE, R.PROMO_NAME, R.DISCOUNT_PCT;


CREATE VIEW V_ORDER_FULFILLMENT_STATUS AS
SELECT O.ORDER_ID,
       O.ORDER_NO,
       O.CUSTNO,
       RTRIM(C.FNAME) || ' ' || RTRIM(C.LNAME) AS CUSTOMER_NAME,
       C.STATE,
       O.ORDER_DATE,
       O.REQUIRED_DATE,
       O.SHIPPED_DATE,
       CASE
         WHEN O.SHIPPED_DATE IS NOT NULL THEN (DAYS(O.SHIPPED_DATE) - DAYS(O.ORDER_DATE))
         ELSE NULL
       END AS FULFILLMENT_DAYS,
       O.STATUS,
       O.TOTAL_AMOUNT,
       COUNT(OI.ITEM_ID) AS ITEM_COUNT,
       COALESCE(SUM(OI.QUANTITY), 0) AS TOTAL_UNITS
FROM ORDERS O
     INNER JOIN CUSTOMERS C ON C.CUSTNO = O.CUSTNO
     LEFT OUTER JOIN ORDER_ITEMS OI ON OI.ORDER_ID = O.ORDER_ID
GROUP BY O.ORDER_ID, O.ORDER_NO, O.CUSTNO, C.FNAME, C.LNAME, C.STATE,
         O.ORDER_DATE, O.REQUIRED_DATE, O.SHIPPED_DATE, O.STATUS, O.TOTAL_AMOUNT;


CREATE VIEW V_INVENTORY_RESTOCK_ALERT AS
SELECT I.WAREHOUSE_ID,
       P.PRODUCT_ID,
       P.SKU,
       P.PRODUCT_NAME,
       I.ON_HAND_QTY,
       I.ALLOCATED_QTY,
       (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) AS AVAILABLE_QTY,
       I.REORDER_POINT,
       I.REORDER_QTY,
       I.SAFETY_STOCK,
       I.BIN_LOCATION,
       CASE
         WHEN (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) <= I.SAFETY_STOCK THEN 'CRITICAL'
         WHEN (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) <= I.REORDER_POINT THEN 'REORDER_NOW'
         ELSE 'HEALTHY'
       END AS INVENTORY_STATUS
FROM INVENTORY I
     INNER JOIN PRODUCTS P ON P.PRODUCT_ID = I.PRODUCT_ID
WHERE (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) <= I.REORDER_POINT;


CREATE VIEW V_CUSTOMER_360_ORDERS AS
SELECT C.CUSTNO,
       RTRIM(C.FNAME) || ' ' || RTRIM(C.LNAME) AS CUSTOMER_NAME,
       C.CITY,
       C.STATE,
       COUNT(O.ORDER_ID) AS TOTAL_ORDERS,
       COALESCE(SUM(O.TOTAL_AMOUNT), 0.00) AS LIFETIME_ORDER_VALUE,
       MAX(O.ORDER_DATE) AS LAST_ORDER_DATE,
       SUM(CASE WHEN O.STATUS IN ('PENDING', 'PROCESSING') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS OPEN_ORDERS_COUNT
FROM CUSTOMERS C
     LEFT OUTER JOIN ORDERS O ON O.CUSTNO = C.CUSTNO
GROUP BY C.CUSTNO, C.FNAME, C.LNAME, C.CITY, C.STATE;

CREATE PROCEDURE SP_ADD_CUSTOMER (
  IN  P_CUSTNO  CHAR(6),

CREATE PROCEDURE SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE (
  OUT P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT INTEGER,
  OUT P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  INTEGER
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_ON_HAND      INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_ALLOCATED    INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_REORDER_PT   INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_AVAIL        INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_AT_END       SMALLINT DEFAULT 0;--

  DECLARE C_SHORTAGE CURSOR FOR
    SELECT ON_HAND_QTY, ALLOCATED_QTY, REORDER_POINT
      FROM INVENTORY
     WHERE (ON_HAND_QTY - ALLOCATED_QTY) < REORDER_POINT;--

  DECLARE CONTINUE HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SET V_AT_END = 1;--

  SET P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT = 0;--
  SET P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  = 0;--

  OPEN C_SHORTAGE;--
  FETCH C_SHORTAGE INTO V_ON_HAND, V_ALLOCATED, V_REORDER_PT;--

  WHILE V_AT_END = 0 DO
    SET V_AVAIL = V_ON_HAND - V_ALLOCATED;--
    SET P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT = P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT + 1;--
    SET P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  = P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT + (V_REORDER_PT - V_AVAIL);--

    FETCH C_SHORTAGE INTO V_ON_HAND, V_ALLOCATED, V_REORDER_PT;--
  END WHILE;--

  CLOSE C_SHORTAGE;--
END;--;


CREATE PROCEDURE SP_PLACE_ORDER (
  IN  P_CUSTNO         CHAR(6),
  IN  P_ORDER_NO       CHAR(8),
  IN  P_PAYMENT_METHOD VARCHAR(20),
  IN  P_SUBTOTAL       DECIMAL(11,2),
  OUT P_ORDER_ID       INTEGER,
  OUT P_TOTAL_AMOUNT   DECIMAL(11,2)
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CUST_EXISTS INTEGER DEFAULT 0;--
  DECLARE V_TAX         DECIMAL(9,2) DEFAULT 0.00;--
  DECLARE V_FREIGHT     DECIMAL(9,2) DEFAULT 15.00;--
  DECLARE V_STATE       CHAR(2);--
  DECLARE CUST_MISSING  CONDITION FOR SQLSTATE '75002';--

  DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SIGNAL CUST_MISSING SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Customer does not exist in CUSTOMERS table';--

  SELECT STATE INTO V_STATE
    FROM CUSTOMERS
   WHERE CUSTNO = P_CUSTNO;--

  -- Apply 6% tax for TX, 7% for CA/NY
  IF V_STATE = 'TX' THEN
    SET V_TAX = ROUND(P_SUBTOTAL * 0.06, 2);--
  ELSEIF V_STATE IN ('CA', 'NY') THEN
    SET V_TAX = ROUND(P_SUBTOTAL * 0.07, 2);--
  ELSE
    SET V_TAX = 0.00;--
  END IF;--

  SET P_TOTAL_AMOUNT = P_SUBTOTAL + V_TAX + V_FREIGHT;--

  INSERT INTO ORDERS (
    ORDER_NO,
    CUSTNO,
    ORDER_DATE,
    REQUIRED_DATE,
    STATUS,
    SUBTOTAL,
    TAX_AMOUNT,
    FREIGHT_CHARGE,
    TOTAL_AMOUNT,
    PAYMENT_METHOD,
    PAYMENT_STATUS
  ) VALUES (
    P_ORDER_NO,
    P_CUSTNO,
    CURRENT DATE,
    CURRENT DATE + 7 DAYS,
    'PENDING',
    P_SUBTOTAL,
    V_TAX,
    V_FREIGHT,
    P_TOTAL_AMOUNT,
    P_PAYMENT_METHOD,
    'AUTHORIZED'
  );--

  SELECT ORDER_ID INTO P_ORDER_ID
    FROM ORDERS
   WHERE ORDER_NO = P_ORDER_NO;--

END;--
;


CREATE PROCEDURE SP_REFRESH_CUSTOMER_SUMMARY (OUT P_ROWS INTEGER)
  LANGUAGE SQL
  MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CUSTNO  CHAR(6);--
  DECLARE V_COUNT   INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_TOTAL   DECIMAL(11,2);--
  DECLARE V_LAST    DATE;--
  DECLARE V_AT_END  SMALLINT DEFAULT 0;--

  DECLARE C1 CURSOR FOR
    SELECT INVCUST, COUNT(*), SUM(INVTOTAL), MAX(INVDATE)
      FROM INVOICES
     GROUP BY INVCUST
     ORDER BY INVCUST;--

  DECLARE CONTINUE HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SET V_AT_END = 1;--

  SET P_ROWS = 0;--

  DELETE FROM CUSTOMER_SALES_SUMMARY;--

  OPEN C1;--
  FETCH C1 INTO V_CUSTNO, V_COUNT, V_TOTAL, V_LAST;--

  WHILE V_AT_END = 0 DO
    INSERT INTO CUSTOMER_SALES_SUMMARY
           (CUSTNO, INVOICE_COUNT, TOTAL_SALES, LAST_INVOICE_DATE, REFRESHED_TS)
    VALUES (V_CUSTNO, V_COUNT, V_TOTAL, V_LAST, CURRENT TIMESTAMP);--

    SET P_ROWS = P_ROWS + 1;--
    FETCH C1 INTO V_CUSTNO, V_COUNT, V_TOTAL, V_LAST;--
  END WHILE;--

  CLOSE C1;--
END;--;


CREATE PROCEDURE SP_RESTOCK_INVENTORY (
  IN  P_WAREHOUSE_ID   CHAR(4),
  IN  P_PRODUCT_ID     INTEGER,
  IN  P_RESTOCK_QTY    INTEGER,
  IN  P_OPERATOR_ID    VARCHAR(20),
  IN  P_PO_NUMBER      VARCHAR(30),
  OUT P_NEW_ON_HAND    INTEGER
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CURRENT_QTY INTEGER;--
  DECLARE INV_NOT_FOUND CONDITION FOR SQLSTATE '75003';--

  DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SIGNAL INV_NOT_FOUND SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Warehouse product inventory record not found';--

  SELECT ON_HAND_QTY INTO V_CURRENT_QTY
    FROM INVENTORY
   WHERE WAREHOUSE_ID = P_WAREHOUSE_ID
     AND PRODUCT_ID = P_PRODUCT_ID;--

  SET P_NEW_ON_HAND = V_CURRENT_QTY + P_RESTOCK_QTY;--

  UPDATE INVENTORY
     SET ON_HAND_QTY = P_NEW_ON_HAND,
         LAST_RESTOCK_DATE = CURRENT DATE,
         LAST_AUDIT_TS = CURRENT TIMESTAMP
   WHERE WAREHOUSE_ID = P_WAREHOUSE_ID
     AND PRODUCT_ID = P_PRODUCT_ID;--

  INSERT INTO INVENTORY_TRANSACTIONS (
    PRODUCT_ID,
    WAREHOUSE_ID,
    TXN_TYPE,
    QUANTITY,
    REFERENCE_NO,
    OPERATOR_ID,
    NOTES
  ) VALUES (
    P_PRODUCT_ID,
    P_WAREHOUSE_ID,
    'RECEIPT',
    P_RESTOCK_QTY,
    P_PO_NUMBER,
    P_OPERATOR_ID,
    'Restock replenishment processed successfully'
  );--

END;--;

CREATE VIEW V_CUSTOMER_INVOICES AS
SELECT C.CUSTNO,
       RTRIM(C.FNAME) || ' ' || RTRIM(C.LNAME) AS CUSTOMER_NAME,
       C.STATE,
       I.INVNO,
       I.INVDATE,
       I.INVTOTAL,
       I.INVPROM
FROM CUSTOMERS C
     INNER JOIN INVOICES I
     ON I.INVCUST = C.CUSTNO;


CREATE VIEW V_INVOICE_DETAIL AS
SELECT I.INVNO,
       I.INVDATE,
       I.INVCUST,
       L.LINE_NO,
       P.SKU,
       P.PRODUCT_NAME,
       L.QUANTITY,
       L.UNIT_PRICE,
       L.LINE_TOTAL
FROM INVOICES I
     INNER JOIN INVOICE_LINES L ON L.INVNO = I.INVNO
     INNER JOIN PRODUCTS P ON P.PRODUCT_ID = L.PRODUCT_ID;


CREATE VIEW V_MONTHLY_SALES AS
SELECT YEAR(INVDATE) AS SALES_YEAR,
       MONTH(INVDATE) AS SALES_MONTH,
       COUNT(*) AS INVOICE_COUNT,
       SUM(INVTOTAL) AS TOTAL_SALES,
       AVG(INVTOTAL) AS AVG_INVOICE
FROM INVOICES
GROUP BY YEAR(INVDATE), MONTH(INVDATE);


CREATE VIEW V_PRODUCT_SALES AS
SELECT P.SKU,
       P.PRODUCT_NAME,
       P.CATEGORY,
       COALESCE(SUM(L.QUANTITY), 0) AS UNITS_SOLD,
       COALESCE(SUM(L.LINE_TOTAL), 0) AS REVENUE
FROM PRODUCTS P
     LEFT OUTER JOIN INVOICE_LINES L
     ON L.PRODUCT_ID = P.PRODUCT_ID
GROUP BY P.SKU, P.PRODUCT_NAME, P.CATEGORY;


CREATE VIEW V_PROMO_USAGE AS
SELECT R.PROMO_CODE,
       R.PROMO_NAME,
       R.DISCOUNT_PCT,
       COUNT(I.INVNO) AS INVOICES_USED,
       COALESCE(SUM(I.INVTOTAL), 0) AS SALES_WITH_PROMO
FROM PROMOTIONS R
     LEFT OUTER JOIN INVOICES I
     ON I.INVPROM = R.PROMO_CODE
GROUP BY R.PROMO_CODE, R.PROMO_NAME, R.DISCOUNT_PCT;


CREATE VIEW V_ORDER_FULFILLMENT_STATUS AS
SELECT O.ORDER_ID,
       O.ORDER_NO,
       O.CUSTNO,
       RTRIM(C.FNAME) || ' ' || RTRIM(C.LNAME) AS CUSTOMER_NAME,
       C.STATE,
       O.ORDER_DATE,
       O.REQUIRED_DATE,
       O.SHIPPED_DATE,
       CASE
         WHEN O.SHIPPED_DATE IS NOT NULL THEN (DAYS(O.SHIPPED_DATE) - DAYS(O.ORDER_DATE))
         ELSE NULL
       END AS FULFILLMENT_DAYS,
       O.STATUS,
       O.TOTAL_AMOUNT,
       COUNT(OI.ITEM_ID) AS ITEM_COUNT,
       COALESCE(SUM(OI.QUANTITY), 0) AS TOTAL_UNITS
FROM ORDERS O
     INNER JOIN CUSTOMERS C ON C.CUSTNO = O.CUSTNO
     LEFT OUTER JOIN ORDER_ITEMS OI ON OI.ORDER_ID = O.ORDER_ID
GROUP BY O.ORDER_ID, O.ORDER_NO, O.CUSTNO, C.FNAME, C.LNAME, C.STATE,
         O.ORDER_DATE, O.REQUIRED_DATE, O.SHIPPED_DATE, O.STATUS, O.TOTAL_AMOUNT;


CREATE VIEW V_INVENTORY_RESTOCK_ALERT AS
SELECT I.WAREHOUSE_ID,
       P.PRODUCT_ID,
       P.SKU,
       P.PRODUCT_NAME,
       I.ON_HAND_QTY,
       I.ALLOCATED_QTY,
       (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) AS AVAILABLE_QTY,
       I.REORDER_POINT,
       I.REORDER_QTY,
       I.SAFETY_STOCK,
       I.BIN_LOCATION,
       CASE
         WHEN (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) <= I.SAFETY_STOCK THEN 'CRITICAL'
         WHEN (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) <= I.REORDER_POINT THEN 'REORDER_NOW'
         ELSE 'HEALTHY'
       END AS INVENTORY_STATUS
FROM INVENTORY I
     INNER JOIN PRODUCTS P ON P.PRODUCT_ID = I.PRODUCT_ID
WHERE (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) <= I.REORDER_POINT;


CREATE VIEW V_CUSTOMER_360_ORDERS AS
SELECT C.CUSTNO,
       RTRIM(C.FNAME) || ' ' || RTRIM(C.LNAME) AS CUSTOMER_NAME,
       C.CITY,
       C.STATE,
       COUNT(O.ORDER_ID) AS TOTAL_ORDERS,
       COALESCE(SUM(O.TOTAL_AMOUNT), 0.00) AS LIFETIME_ORDER_VALUE,
       MAX(O.ORDER_DATE) AS LAST_ORDER_DATE,
       SUM(CASE WHEN O.STATUS IN ('PENDING', 'PROCESSING') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS OPEN_ORDERS_COUNT
FROM CUSTOMERS C
     LEFT OUTER JOIN ORDERS O ON O.CUSTNO = C.CUSTNO
GROUP BY C.CUSTNO, C.FNAME, C.LNAME, C.CITY, C.STATE;

CREATE PROCEDURE SP_ADD_CUSTOMER (
  IN  P_CUSTNO  CHAR(6),
  IN  P_FNAME   VARCHAR(20),
  IN  P_LNAME   VARCHAR(30),
  IN  P_ADDR    VARCHAR(30),
  IN  P_CITY    VARCHAR(20),

BEGIN
  DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR SQLSTATE '23505'
    SET P_STATUS = -1;--
  DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR SQLEXCEPTION
    SET P_STATUS = -99;--

  SET P_STATUS = 0;--

  INSERT INTO CUSTOMERS (CUSTNO, FNAME, LNAME, ADDR, CITY, STATE, ZIPCODE)
  VALUES (P_CUSTNO, P_FNAME, P_LNAME, P_ADDR, P_CITY, P_STATE, P_ZIP);--

END;


CREATE PROCEDURE SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE (
  OUT P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT INTEGER,
  OUT P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  INTEGER
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_ON_HAND      INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_ALLOCATED    INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_REORDER_PT   INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_AVAIL        INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_AT_END       SMALLINT DEFAULT 0;--

  DECLARE C_SHORTAGE CURSOR FOR
    SELECT ON_HAND_QTY, ALLOCATED_QTY, REORDER_POINT
      FROM INVENTORY
     WHERE (ON_HAND_QTY - ALLOCATED_QTY) < REORDER_POINT;--

  DECLARE CONTINUE HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SET V_AT_END = 1;--

  SET P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT = 0;--
  SET P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  = 0;--

  OPEN C_SHORTAGE;--
  FETCH C_SHORTAGE INTO V_ON_HAND, V_ALLOCATED, V_REORDER_PT;--

  WHILE V_AT_END = 0 DO
    SET V_AVAIL = V_ON_HAND - V_ALLOCATED;--
    SET P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT = P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT + 1;--
    SET P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  = P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT + (V_REORDER_PT - V_AVAIL);--

    FETCH C_SHORTAGE INTO V_ON_HAND, V_ALLOCATED, V_REORDER_PT;--
  END WHILE;--

  CLOSE C_SHORTAGE;--
END;--;


CREATE PROCEDURE SP_PLACE_ORDER (
  IN  P_CUSTNO         CHAR(6),
  IN  P_ORDER_NO       CHAR(8),
  IN  P_PAYMENT_METHOD VARCHAR(20),
  IN  P_SUBTOTAL       DECIMAL(11,2),
  OUT P_ORDER_ID       INTEGER,
  OUT P_TOTAL_AMOUNT   DECIMAL(11,2)
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CUST_EXISTS INTEGER DEFAULT 0;--
  DECLARE V_TAX         DECIMAL(9,2) DEFAULT 0.00;--
  DECLARE V_FREIGHT     DECIMAL(9,2) DEFAULT 15.00;--
  DECLARE V_STATE       CHAR(2);--
  DECLARE CUST_MISSING  CONDITION FOR SQLSTATE '75002';--

  DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SIGNAL CUST_MISSING SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Customer does not exist in CUSTOMERS table';--

  SELECT STATE INTO V_STATE
    FROM CUSTOMERS
   WHERE CUSTNO = P_CUSTNO;--

  -- Apply 6% tax for TX, 7% for CA/NY
  IF V_STATE = 'TX' THEN
    SET V_TAX = ROUND(P_SUBTOTAL * 0.06, 2);--
  ELSEIF V_STATE IN ('CA', 'NY') THEN
    SET V_TAX = ROUND(P_SUBTOTAL * 0.07, 2);--
  ELSE
    SET V_TAX = 0.00;--
  END IF;--

  SET P_TOTAL_AMOUNT = P_SUBTOTAL + V_TAX + V_FREIGHT;--

  INSERT INTO ORDERS (
    ORDER_NO,
    CUSTNO,
    ORDER_DATE,
    REQUIRED_DATE,
    STATUS,
    SUBTOTAL,
    TAX_AMOUNT,
    FREIGHT_CHARGE,
    TOTAL_AMOUNT,
    PAYMENT_METHOD,
    PAYMENT_STATUS
  ) VALUES (
    P_ORDER_NO,
    P_CUSTNO,
    CURRENT DATE,
    CURRENT DATE + 7 DAYS,
    'PENDING',
    P_SUBTOTAL,
    V_TAX,
    V_FREIGHT,
    P_TOTAL_AMOUNT,
    P_PAYMENT_METHOD,
    'AUTHORIZED'
  );--

  SELECT ORDER_ID INTO P_ORDER_ID
    FROM ORDERS
   WHERE ORDER_NO = P_ORDER_NO;--

END;--
;


CREATE PROCEDURE SP_REFRESH_CUSTOMER_SUMMARY (OUT P_ROWS INTEGER)
  LANGUAGE SQL
  MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CUSTNO  CHAR(6);--
  DECLARE V_COUNT   INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_TOTAL   DECIMAL(11,2);--
  DECLARE V_LAST    DATE;--
  DECLARE V_AT_END  SMALLINT DEFAULT 0;--

  DECLARE C1 CURSOR FOR
    SELECT INVCUST, COUNT(*), SUM(INVTOTAL), MAX(INVDATE)
      FROM INVOICES
     GROUP BY INVCUST
     ORDER BY INVCUST;--

  DECLARE CONTINUE HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SET V_AT_END = 1;--

  SET P_ROWS = 0;--

  DELETE FROM CUSTOMER_SALES_SUMMARY;--

  OPEN C1;--
  FETCH C1 INTO V_CUSTNO, V_COUNT, V_TOTAL, V_LAST;--

  WHILE V_AT_END = 0 DO
    INSERT INTO CUSTOMER_SALES_SUMMARY
           (CUSTNO, INVOICE_COUNT, TOTAL_SALES, LAST_INVOICE_DATE, REFRESHED_TS)
    VALUES (V_CUSTNO, V_COUNT, V_TOTAL, V_LAST, CURRENT TIMESTAMP);--

    SET P_ROWS = P_ROWS + 1;--
    FETCH C1 INTO V_CUSTNO, V_COUNT, V_TOTAL, V_LAST;--
  END WHILE;--

  CLOSE C1;--
END;--;


CREATE PROCEDURE SP_RESTOCK_INVENTORY (
  IN  P_WAREHOUSE_ID   CHAR(4),
  IN  P_PRODUCT_ID     INTEGER,
  IN  P_RESTOCK_QTY    INTEGER,
  IN  P_OPERATOR_ID    VARCHAR(20),
  IN  P_PO_NUMBER      VARCHAR(30),
  OUT P_NEW_ON_HAND    INTEGER
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CURRENT_QTY INTEGER;--
  DECLARE INV_NOT_FOUND CONDITION FOR SQLSTATE '75003';--

  DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SIGNAL INV_NOT_FOUND SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Warehouse product inventory record not found';--

  SELECT ON_HAND_QTY INTO V_CURRENT_QTY
    FROM INVENTORY
   WHERE WAREHOUSE_ID = P_WAREHOUSE_ID
     AND PRODUCT_ID = P_PRODUCT_ID;--

  SET P_NEW_ON_HAND = V_CURRENT_QTY + P_RESTOCK_QTY;--

  UPDATE INVENTORY
     SET ON_HAND_QTY = P_NEW_ON_HAND,
         LAST_RESTOCK_DATE = CURRENT DATE,
         LAST_AUDIT_TS = CURRENT TIMESTAMP
   WHERE WAREHOUSE_ID = P_WAREHOUSE_ID
     AND PRODUCT_ID = P_PRODUCT_ID;--

  INSERT INTO INVENTORY_TRANSACTIONS (
    PRODUCT_ID,
    WAREHOUSE_ID,
    TXN_TYPE,
    QUANTITY,
    REFERENCE_NO,
    OPERATOR_ID,
    NOTES
  ) VALUES (
    P_PRODUCT_ID,
    P_WAREHOUSE_ID,
    'RECEIPT',
    P_RESTOCK_QTY,
    P_PO_NUMBER,
    P_OPERATOR_ID,
    'Restock replenishment processed successfully'
  );--

END;--;


CREATE PROCEDURE SP_UPDATE_CUSTOMER_ADDRESS (
  IN  P_CUSTNO  CHAR(6),
  IN  P_ADDR    VARCHAR(30),
  IN  P_CITY    VARCHAR(20),
  IN  P_STATE   CHAR(2),
  IN  P_ZIP     VARCHAR(10),
  OUT P_ROWS    INTEGER)
  LANGUAGE SQL
  MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_ROWS INTEGER DEFAULT 0;--

  UPDATE CUSTOMERS
     SET ADDR    = P_ADDR,
         CITY    = P_CITY,
         STATE   = P_STATE,
         ZIPCODE = P_ZIP
   WHERE CUSTNO = P_CUSTNO;--

  GET DIAGNOSTICS V_ROWS = ROW_COUNT;--

  IF V_ROWS > 0 THEN
    INSERT INTO CUSTOMER_AUDIT (CUSTNO, ACTION_CD, NOTES)
    VALUES (P_CUSTNO, 'U', 'Address changed');--
  END IF;--

  SET P_ROWS = V_ROWS;--
END;--;

COMMIT WORK;

TERMINATE;

GROUP BY YEAR(INVDATE), MONTH(INVDATE);


CREATE VIEW V_PRODUCT_SALES AS
SELECT P.SKU,
       P.PRODUCT_NAME,
       P.CATEGORY,
       COALESCE(SUM(L.QUANTITY), 0) AS UNITS_SOLD,
       COALESCE(SUM(L.LINE_TOTAL), 0) AS REVENUE
FROM PRODUCTS P
     LEFT OUTER JOIN INVOICE_LINES L
     ON L.PRODUCT_ID = P.PRODUCT_ID
GROUP BY P.SKU, P.PRODUCT_NAME, P.CATEGORY;


CREATE VIEW V_PROMO_USAGE AS
SELECT R.PROMO_CODE,
       R.PROMO_NAME,
       R.DISCOUNT_PCT,
       COUNT(I.INVNO) AS INVOICES_USED,
       COALESCE(SUM(I.INVTOTAL), 0) AS SALES_WITH_PROMO
FROM PROMOTIONS R
     LEFT OUTER JOIN INVOICES I
     ON I.INVPROM = R.PROMO_CODE
GROUP BY R.PROMO_CODE, R.PROMO_NAME, R.DISCOUNT_PCT;


CREATE VIEW V_ORDER_FULFILLMENT_STATUS AS
SELECT O.ORDER_ID,
       O.ORDER_NO,
       O.CUSTNO,
       RTRIM(C.FNAME) || ' ' || RTRIM(C.LNAME) AS CUSTOMER_NAME,
       C.STATE,
       O.ORDER_DATE,
       O.REQUIRED_DATE,
       O.SHIPPED_DATE,
       CASE
         WHEN O.SHIPPED_DATE IS NOT NULL THEN (DAYS(O.SHIPPED_DATE) - DAYS(O.ORDER_DATE))
         ELSE NULL
       END AS FULFILLMENT_DAYS,
       O.STATUS,
       O.TOTAL_AMOUNT,
       COUNT(OI.ITEM_ID) AS ITEM_COUNT,
       COALESCE(SUM(OI.QUANTITY), 0) AS TOTAL_UNITS
FROM ORDERS O
     INNER JOIN CUSTOMERS C ON C.CUSTNO = O.CUSTNO
     LEFT OUTER JOIN ORDER_ITEMS OI ON OI.ORDER_ID = O.ORDER_ID
GROUP BY O.ORDER_ID, O.ORDER_NO, O.CUSTNO, C.FNAME, C.LNAME, C.STATE,
         O.ORDER_DATE, O.REQUIRED_DATE, O.SHIPPED_DATE, O.STATUS, O.TOTAL_AMOUNT;


CREATE VIEW V_INVENTORY_RESTOCK_ALERT AS
SELECT I.WAREHOUSE_ID,
       P.PRODUCT_ID,
       P.SKU,
       P.PRODUCT_NAME,
       I.ON_HAND_QTY,
       I.ALLOCATED_QTY,
       (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) AS AVAILABLE_QTY,
       I.REORDER_POINT,
       I.REORDER_QTY,
       I.SAFETY_STOCK,
       I.BIN_LOCATION,
       CASE
         WHEN (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) <= I.SAFETY_STOCK THEN 'CRITICAL'
         WHEN (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) <= I.REORDER_POINT THEN 'REORDER_NOW'
         ELSE 'HEALTHY'
       END AS INVENTORY_STATUS
FROM INVENTORY I
     INNER JOIN PRODUCTS P ON P.PRODUCT_ID = I.PRODUCT_ID
WHERE (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) <= I.REORDER_POINT;


CREATE VIEW V_CUSTOMER_360_ORDERS AS
SELECT C.CUSTNO,
       RTRIM(C.FNAME) || ' ' || RTRIM(C.LNAME) AS CUSTOMER_NAME,
       C.CITY,
       C.STATE,
       COUNT(O.ORDER_ID) AS TOTAL_ORDERS,
       COALESCE(SUM(O.TOTAL_AMOUNT), 0.00) AS LIFETIME_ORDER_VALUE,
       MAX(O.ORDER_DATE) AS LAST_ORDER_DATE,
       SUM(CASE WHEN O.STATUS IN ('PENDING', 'PROCESSING') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS OPEN_ORDERS_COUNT
FROM CUSTOMERS C
     LEFT OUTER JOIN ORDERS O ON O.CUSTNO = C.CUSTNO
GROUP BY C.CUSTNO, C.FNAME, C.LNAME, C.CITY, C.STATE;

CREATE PROCEDURE SP_ADD_CUSTOMER (
  IN  P_CUSTNO  CHAR(6),
  IN  P_FNAME   VARCHAR(20),
  IN  P_LNAME   VARCHAR(30),
  IN  P_ADDR    VARCHAR(30),
  IN  P_CITY    VARCHAR(20),

  VALUES (P_CUSTNO, P_FNAME, P_LNAME, P_ADDR, P_CITY, P_STATE, P_ZIP);--
