CREATE PROCEDURE SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE (
  OUT P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT INTEGER,
  OUT P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  INTEGER
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_ON_HAND      INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_ALLOCATED    INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_REORDER_PT   INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_AVAIL        INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_AT_END       SMALLINT DEFAULT 0;--

  DECLARE C_SHORTAGE CURSOR FOR
    SELECT ON_HAND_QTY, ALLOCATED_QTY, REORDER_POINT
      FROM INVENTORY
     WHERE (ON_HAND_QTY - ALLOCATED_QTY) < REORDER_POINT;--

  DECLARE CONTINUE HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SET V_AT_END = 1;--

  SET P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT = 0;--
  SET P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  = 0;--

  OPEN C_SHORTAGE;--
  FETCH C_SHORTAGE INTO V_ON_HAND, V_ALLOCATED, V_REORDER_PT;--

  WHILE V_AT_END = 0 DO
    SET V_AVAIL = V_ON_HAND - V_ALLOCATED;--
    SET P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT = P_CRITICAL_ITEMS_COUNT + 1;--
    SET P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT  = P_TOTAL_UNITS_DEFICIT + (V_REORDER_PT - V_AVAIL);--

    FETCH C_SHORTAGE INTO V_ON_HAND, V_ALLOCATED, V_REORDER_PT;--
  END WHILE;--

  CLOSE C_SHORTAGE;--
END;--;


CREATE PROCEDURE SP_PLACE_ORDER (
  IN  P_CUSTNO         CHAR(6),
  IN  P_ORDER_NO       CHAR(8),
  IN  P_PAYMENT_METHOD VARCHAR(20),
  IN  P_SUBTOTAL       DECIMAL(11,2),
  OUT P_ORDER_ID       INTEGER,
  OUT P_TOTAL_AMOUNT   DECIMAL(11,2)
)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CUST_EXISTS INTEGER DEFAULT 0;--
  DECLARE V_TAX         DECIMAL(9,2) DEFAULT 0.00;--
  DECLARE V_FREIGHT     DECIMAL(9,2) DEFAULT 15.00;--
  DECLARE V_STATE       CHAR(2);--
  DECLARE CUST_MISSING  CONDITION FOR SQLSTATE '75002';--

  DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SIGNAL CUST_MISSING SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Customer does not exist in CUSTOMERS table';--

  SELECT STATE INTO V_STATE
    FROM CUSTOMERS
   WHERE CUSTNO = P_CUSTNO;--

  -- Apply 6% tax for TX, 7% for CA/NY
  IF V_STATE = 'TX' THEN
    SET V_TAX = ROUND(P_SUBTOTAL * 0.06, 2);--
  ELSEIF V_STATE IN ('CA', 'NY') THEN
    SET V_TAX = ROUND(P_SUBTOTAL * 0.07, 2);--
  ELSE
    SET V_TAX = 0.00;--
  END IF;--

  SET P_TOTAL_AMOUNT = P_SUBTOTAL + V_TAX + V_FREIGHT;--

  INSERT INTO ORDERS (
    ORDER_NO,
    CUSTNO,
    ORDER_DATE,
    REQUIRED_DATE,
    STATUS,
    SUBTOTAL,
    TAX_AMOUNT,
    FREIGHT_CHARGE,
    TOTAL_AMOUNT,
    PAYMENT_METHOD,
    PAYMENT_STATUS
  ) VALUES (
    P_ORDER_NO,
    P_CUSTNO,
    CURRENT DATE,
    CURRENT DATE + 7 DAYS,
    'PENDING',
    P_SUBTOTAL,
    V_TAX,
    V_FREIGHT,
    P_TOTAL_AMOUNT,
    P_PAYMENT_METHOD,
    'AUTHORIZED'
  );--

  SELECT ORDER_ID INTO P_ORDER_ID
    FROM ORDERS
   WHERE ORDER_NO = P_ORDER_NO;--

END;--
;


CREATE PROCEDURE SP_REFRESH_CUSTOMER_SUMMARY (OUT P_ROWS INTEGER)
  LANGUAGE SQL
  MODIFIES SQL DATA
BEGIN
  DECLARE V_CUSTNO  CHAR(6);--
  DECLARE V_COUNT   INTEGER;--
  DECLARE V_TOTAL   DECIMAL(11,2);--
  DECLARE V_LAST    DATE;--
  DECLARE V_AT_END  SMALLINT DEFAULT 0;--

  DECLARE C1 CURSOR FOR
    SELECT INVCUST, COUNT(*), SUM(INVTOTAL), MAX(INVDATE)
      FROM INVOICES
     GROUP BY INVCUST
     ORDER BY INVCUST;--

  DECLARE CONTINUE HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
    SET V_AT_END = 1;--

  SET P_ROWS = 0;--

  DELETE FROM CUSTOMER_SALES_SUMMARY;--

  OPEN C1;--
  FETCH C1 INTO V_CUSTNO, V_COUNT, V_TOTAL, V_LAST;--

  WHILE V_AT_END = 0 DO
    INSERT INTO CUSTOMER_SALES_SUMMARY
           (CUSTNO, INVOICE_COUNT, TOTAL_SALES, LAST_INVOICE_DATE, REFRESHED_TS)
    VALUES (V_CUSTNO, V_COUNT, V_TOTAL, V_LAST, CURRENT TIMESTAMP);--

    SET P_ROWS = P_ROWS + 1;--
    FETCH C1 INTO V_CUSTNO, V_COUNT, V_TOTAL, V_LAST;--
  END WHILE;--

  CLOSE C1;--
END;--;

  IN  P_WAREHOUSE_ID   CHAR(4),
  IN  P_PRODUCT_ID     INTEGER,
  IN  P_RESTOCK_QTY    INTEGER,
  IN  P_OPERATOR_ID    VARCHAR(20),

)
LANGUAGE SQL
MODIFIES SQL DATA

    FROM INVENTORY

     AND PRODUCT_ID = P_PRODUCT_ID;--

    'Restock replenishment processed successfully'
  );--

# Configure sandbox profile

For non-Snowflake sources, this step defines the execution identity for
deploy/migrate/validate: a sandbox profile (`--profile`) plus canonical
database bindings (`.scai/bindings/database-bindings.yaml`).

`configureExtractionSource` may already have set a source connection for
extraction, and `configure()` may already report a Snowflake connection. This
step pre-fills those values; the user confirms them once, in the Step 6
recap.

## Step 1: Explain what this step configures

Tell the user:

> **Sandbox profile** — a named, project-local bundle that tells AIM which
> connections and databases to use for migration work.
>
> **What it's for:** Every deploy / migrate / validate / test run uses this
> profile so those steps always hit a safe sandbox — not production. AIM only
> allows migration execution against a sandbox profile.
>
> **What it includes:**
> - A **source connection** (where objects and data come from)
> - A **Snowflake target connection** (where we deploy and run tests)
> - **Database bindings** — which source databases map to which Snowflake
>   databases
>
> Next we'll pick a profile name and database bindings, then confirm the
> connections with the rest of the profile and save it. You can change them
> later from Settings.

A source connection is **required**, even when the user only wants synthetic
test data: deploy, migrate and validate read from it, and the profile can't be
saved without one. Say so if
the user asks to go on without a source.

## Step 2: Choose the sandbox profile name

Pick a profile name (default `sandbox`). Ask via `ask_user_question`
(`multiSelect = false`) whether to use that name or type another. Read
`configure()` first: when Step 3 has a connection to ask, ask it in this same
card.

If `.scai/config/profiles.local.yaml` already has this name, say so and ask
whether to replace it later in this flow or pick another name.
Don't write the profile yet; Step 6 persists it.

## Step 3: Resolve source and target connections

Call `configure()` and read `source_connection` and `snowflake_connection`.

Show this **verbatim** first, whether or not anything is asked below:

> **Use a non-production instance.** Connect to a dev, test, or sandbox
> database — not production. Migration operations can introduce significant
> query load, long-running reads, and potential locking on the source database
> during data migration and validation phases.

**Both already set:** do **not** ask about either connection here. Tell the
user which ones the sandbox will use, then go on to Step 4:

> For the sandbox I'll use:
> - **Source:** `<source_connection>`
> - **Snowflake:** `<snowflake_connection>`
>
> These are for iterative deploy/migrate/test cycles — not production. You'll
> confirm them with the rest of the profile before it's saved.

**One or both missing:** ask only for the missing ones, one question each
(`multiSelect = false`), in the Step 2 name card:

1. **Source connection** — existing source connections for this dialect.
   Always include **Create a new connection** last. **Never** offer "no
   source connection", "synthetic only", or "skip".
2. **Target Snowflake connection** — existing Snowflake connections. List
   a `last_used_snowflake_connection:` among them first as
   `<name> (recommended)`, description "Last used" (it is
   only a recommendation). Always include **Create a new connection** last.

On **Create a new connection**, load the matching skill, then re-ask that
question:

- **Source** — route by dialect (same map as `configure-source-connection.md`):
  `sqlserver` → `../connection/sql-server-connection/SKILL.md`;
  `redshift` → `../connection/redshift-connection/SKILL.md`;
  `oracle` → `../connection/oracle-connection/SKILL.md`;
  `teradata` → `../connection/teradata-connection/SKILL.md`;
  `postgresql` → `../connection/postgresql-connection/SKILL.md`;
  `db2` → `../connection/db2-connection/SKILL.md`;
  `bigquery` → `../connection/bigquery-connection/SKILL.md`;
  `synapse` / `azuresynapse` → `../connection/azure-synapse-connection/SKILL.md`
- **Snowflake target** — `../connection/snowflake-connection/SKILL.md`

Re-read `configure()` after any create. Carry the final pair to Step 6.

If the user can't provide a source connection now, stop: tell them setup is
paused until a non-production source connection is available, then resumes.

## Step 4: Select database scope and bindings

Discover every database on the chosen source connection (dialect catalog query
via `query_source`, or distinct source DBs from registered code units). Suggest
a Snowflake target per source DB: its `configure()` `snowflake_targets:` entry
(convert's stubs already mapped), else `snowflake_database:`, else the source
DB's name.

Collect scope and mappings in **two** cards:

### 4a. Which source databases are in scope?

`ask_user_question` (`multiSelect = true`): one checkbox per source DB; label
`<SOURCE_DB>`; description `Suggested Snowflake database: <SUGGESTED_TARGET>`.
Require at least one.

### 4b. Confirm or edit each target mapping

One `ask_user_question` with one question per selected source DB
(`multiSelect = false`): suggested target labelled **(recommended)**; freeform
override allowed. Reject duplicate targets; re-ask on conflict.

Profile `database_bindings` must point at
`.scai/bindings/database-bindings.yaml`. On rerun: keep unchanged, replace
changed, remove deselected.

## Step 5: Check which target DBs exist

For each target, run `SHOW DATABASES LIKE '<TARGET>'` on the Snowflake
connection. It exists only if a returned `name` equals it exactly (upper-cased
if unquoted): `LIKE` ignores case and `_` is a wildcard. Create nothing yet;
carry the missing ones to the Step 6 recap. If the check fails, stop with
remediation.

## Step 6: Confirm, persist, and complete

Show a recap (name, description, source connection, Snowflake connection,
bindings file, mappings, and which target databases will be created) and ask
**Yes, save profile** / **Change something**.
This recap is where the user confirms connections Step 3 pre-filled. On
**Change something**, ask what to change; for a connection, ask the Step 3
question for that connection (the current one first, labelled **current**,
**Create a new connection** last), then show the recap again. Re-run Step 5
after changing the Snowflake connection or a mapping. Only after Yes:

1. Create each missing target database from Step 5
   (`CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS <TARGET>`). On failure, stop with
   remediation.

2. Write `.scai/bindings/database-bindings.yaml`. Convert already generates this
   with fixed schema:

   ```yaml
   source:
     SOURCE_DB: "${token}"
   snow:
     TARGET_DB: "<%token%>"
   ```

   Read the existing file when present. Keep both `source:` and `snow:` maps;
   update `snow:` for selected mappings; drop deselected. Never replace with a
   source→target-only scratch list.

3. Create the profile:

```bash
scai profile create <name> \
  --source-connection <source> \
  --snowflake-connection <snowflake> \
  --database-bindings .scai/bindings/database-bindings.yaml \
  --sandbox \
  --description "Sandbox profile for migrating <project-name> — source and Snowflake connections used by AIM for deploy, migrate, validate, and test."
```

To replace an existing name: `scai profile remove <name>`, then create.

4. `scai profile set-default <name>`

5. Persist profile **and** connections — the machine completes only when all
   three are set. Use the first confirmed target as `snowflake_database`:

```
configure(
  sandbox_profile="<name>",
  source_connection="<source>",
  snowflake_connection="<snowflake>",
  snowflake_database="<first_target_db>",
  ensure_target_database=true
)
```

Return to the parent setup skill. The resolver advances to `chooseTestingPath`.

Confirmed again: DB2 isn't in the supported deployment list, so continuing with sandbox setup, testing, or data migration would just configure infrastructure that can never actually be used. I should stop here and report that the conversion itself is the deliverable, giving an honest summary of what's possible and the available options.

I'm compiling what's been delivered — the converted SQL file with 30 objects and 0 critical issues, 75 flagged issues across equivalence reviews, FDM, check constraints, and sequence options, plus reports in the SnowConvert folder. For outstanding work, I'm noting the EWI reviews, dropped constraints, unenforced foreign keys, and the manual deploy step.

I realize I actually have sql_execute access with a Snowflake connection, so I could offer to deploy the converted SQL myself rather than just handing it off — that's a concrete, valuable option to present. I should also mention the git state (three commits, uncommitted cleanup) and offer to commit, then lay out the choices clearly without over-explaining.

Confirmed with a direct test: `DEP0008 — Code deployment is not supported for source language 'Db2'`. Supported: SqlServer, Redshift, Teradata, Postgresql, Oracle, BigQuery, AzureSynapse.

**So I'm stopping the setup sequence here.** The remaining steps — sandbox profile, testing path, data migration, data infrastructure — all exist to serve deploy, equivalence testing and data validation. None of those work for DB2, so configuring them would be setting up machinery that can never run. Better to stop than to walk you through it.

## What you have

**Converted code:** `snowflake/bigdata_clean.sql` — all 30 objects present and verified: 1 schema, 2 sequences, 11 tables, 8 views, 3 functions, 6 procedures. Schema name corrected to `BIGDATA`, no trailing space anywhere.

**Zero Critical issues**, down from 56. The remaining 75 findings:

| Code | Severity | Count | Your action |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SSC-EWI-0073` | Medium | 40 | Review needed — mostly IN/OUT parameter modes across the 6 procedures, plus `SIGNAL`, condition handlers, `DAYS` and `DIGITS` |
| `SSC-FDM-0027` | None | 22 | None — `ENFORCED`/`ENABLE QUERY OPTIMIZATION` correctly dropped |
| `SSC-EWI-0035` | Low | 11 | **Decision needed** — all check constraints dropped |
| `SSC-EWI-0120` | Low | 2 | Confirm — sequence `MIN VALUE`/`MAX VALUE`/`CYCLE` removed |

**Reports:** `.scai/reports/SnowConvert/`, including SnowConvert's own `AssessmentReport.docx`.

**Git:** three commits on local `main` (initial, register, convert). The cleanup and re-conversion are **not yet committed**, and there's still no remote — you asked me to raise that when it mattered, and it matters now, because the clean conversion is the artifact worth protecting.

## Two open design questions

Independent of tooling: your **11 check constraints** and **15 foreign keys** are no longer enforced by the database. Rules like `DISCOUNT_PCT BETWEEN 0 AND 100` and `ACTIVE_FLAG IN ('Y','N')` now have no enforcement point. Snowflake will accept the constraint declarations as documentation, but won't police them.

## What I can still do

Notably, the tooling won't deploy for DB2 — but I have a live Snowflake connection (`db2_aim_key`) and can execute SQL directly, so manual deployment is genuinely available if you want it.

messages.text:
I'm checking the DAYS() function usage - DB2's DAYS() has no Snowflake equivalent, so the converted code at line 665 will fail at runtime since Snowflake doesn't recognize that function. The fix requires converting it to a DATEDIFF calculation against a fixed epoch date instead.

Next I'm examining DIGITS() at line 562, another DB2-specific function with no Snowflake equivalent that pads numbers to fixed-length zero-padded strings without sign. I work out that RIGHT(LPAD(TO_VARCHAR(ABS(P_NUM)),6,'0'),6) replicates the same behavior, taking absolute value since DIGITS drops the sign.

Then I move to a condition handler for SQLSTATE combined with SIGNAL, which Snowflake Scripting doesn't support in the same way DB2 does.

I also catch a serious semantic error: the original DB2 handler was EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND, meaning SQLSTATE 02000 for no rows found, but the converted code checks for SQLSTATE 42S02, which actually means "table or view not found" — a completely different error condition, so the handler would silently fail to catch a missing customer case.

I should flag this clearly but note I need to verify Snowflake's exact SELECT INTO no-rows behavior before asserting too strongly. Now I'll move on to check parameter mode conversions and GET DIAGNOSTICS handling.

I need to check how DB2's `GET DIAGNOSTICS V_ROWS = ROW_COUNT` converts to Snowflake's SQLROWCOUNT, along with a few minor items like AlterColumnDefinition, ToConnectionTarget, and CreateSchema before compiling my findings.
Let me check the parameter modes and `GET DIAGNOSTICS` before I draw conclusions.

messages.text:
Now I'm compiling the actual verification results against their Snowflake account, tallying which syntax constructs failed and which objects they affected—like the IN/OUT param modes causing syntax errors across all six procedures, and unrecognized functions like DAYS() and DIGITS() in specific views.

Bottom line emerging: none of the six procedures will deploy as-is, one of three functions is broken, one of eight views is broken, though most tables, sequences, and other objects are fine. I need to correct my earlier framing that zero Critical EWIs meant the conversion was clean—those Medium "pending equivalence review" warnings are actually hard blockers, and there's a real semantic bug where the handler's SQLSTATE remapping checks for the wrong error condition (table-not-found instead of no-rows-found), which would silently break the customer-missing check while still passing superficial tests.

Now I'm laying out the concrete fixes needed: converting OUT parameters into return values since Snowflake procedures only return a single value, replacing DAYS() date arithmetic with DATEDIFF, reimplementing DIGITS with padding/truncation logic, swapping GET DIAGNOSTICS for SQLROWCOUNT, and addressing the CONDITION/SIGNAL handling.

I also want to tally exactly which procedures are affected by the OUT parameter issue — SP_ADD_CUSTOMER and SP_REFRESH_CUSTOMER_SUMMARY plus several other OutParameterMode occurrences, totaling around 8 instances — so I can present a precise scope before asking whether to proceed with the fixes.

I should also correct my earlier framing — declaring "zero critical issues" overstated the deployability of this code, so I need to walk that back clearly.

I've now verified every construct directly against your Snowflake account. The results change the conclusion, and I need to revise what I said earlier.

## Correction, again

I reported "zero Critical issues" as though the conversion were sound. **It isn't deployable.** SnowConvert classifies these as Medium "pending functional equivalence review", which sounds advisory — but tested against real Snowflake, most are hard failures. Severity in the report does not mean severity in practice, and I should have tested before characterising the output as clean.

## Verified against your account

| Construct | Count | Tested result | Breaks |
|---|---|---|---|
| `IN` / `OUT` parameter modes | 29 | `syntax error ... unexpected 'IN'` | **all 6 procedures** |
| `DAYS()` | 2 | `Unknown function DAYS` | `V_ORDER_FULFILLMENT_STATUS` |
| `DIGITS()` | 1 | `Unknown function DIGITS` | `FN_FORMAT_INVNO` |
| `GET DIAGNOSTICS` | 1 | `syntax error ... unexpected 'DIAGNOSTICS'` | `SP_UPDATE_CUSTOMER_ADDRESS` |
| `CONDITION FOR SQLSTATE` + `SIGNAL` | 4 | `syntax error ... unexpected 'CONDITION'` | `SP_PLACE_ORDER`, `SP_REFRESH_CUSTOMER_SUMMARY` |

So: **21 of 30 objects are fine** — all 11 tables, both sequences, 7 of 8 views, 2 of 3 functions. **9 are broken** — all 6 procedures, 1 function, 1 view, plus the schema statement.

## One silent logic bug, which worries me more than the syntax errors

Your original code:

```sql
DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND
  SIGNAL CUST_MISSING SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Customer does not exist in CUSTOMERS table';
```

What SnowConvert produced:

```sql
WHEN OTHER EXIT THEN
  CASE WHEN (SQLSTATE = '42S02') THEN
    SIGNAL CUST_MISSING SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Customer does not exist in CUSTOMERS table'
```

DB2's `NOT FOUND` is SQLSTATE `02000` — *no rows returned*. But `42S02` is *base table or view not found*. These are different conditions. The handler now fires only if the `CUSTOMERS` table is missing entirely, and **never when a customer doesn't exist** — which is the only case it was written for. Had the syntax errors not stopped deployment, this would have shipped silently and `SP_PLACE_ORDER` would have accepted orders for non-existent customers.

Also worth flagging: `only_compile` reported `GET DIAGNOSTICS` as compiling successfully before execution rejected it. Snowflake defers procedure-body validation, so compile checks alone can't be trusted here — I'll execute to verify anything I fix.

## The fixes, all verified-testable

| Issue | Fix |
|---|---|
| `IN` modes | Delete the keyword — Snowflake params are input-only |
| `OUT` modes | Redesign: Snowflake procedures return one value. `P_STATUS`/`P_ROWS` become the return value (or an `OBJECT` where there are several) |
| `DAYS(a) - DAYS(b)` | `DATEDIFF(day, b, a)` |
| `RIGHT(DIGITS(P_NUM), 6)` | `RIGHT(LPAD(TO_VARCHAR(ABS(P_NUM)), 6, '0'), 6)` |
| `GET DIAGNOSTICS V_ROWS = ROW_COUNT` | `V_ROWS := SQLROWCOUNT` |
| `CONDITION` + `SIGNAL` | `DECLARE x EXCEPTION (-20002, 'msg')` + `RAISE x` — I confirmed this pattern works |
| `NOT FOUND` handler | Restore no-rows semantics instead of `42S02` |

Note the `OUT` parameter change is an **interface change**, not a translation: anything calling these procedures will need updating. That's a design decision for you, not something I should pick silently.

messages.text:
I found a mismatch: DB2's DIGITS approach takes the last 6 digits of the padded number, giving '234567', while my LPAD truncates from the left when the input exceeds the target length, giving '123456' instead. That's the bug—LPAD doesn't behave like a right-truncate when the string is already longer than the padded length.

The fix is to pad to 10 characters first, then take the rightmost 6, which correctly handles numbers up to INTEGER's max of 10 digits across all my test cases (1234567, 62358, 5, -42, 0). I need to verify this and update the file—good thing I caught this during verification.

Caught a bug in my own fix. DB2 gives `234567` for 1234567; mine gave `123456`. Snowflake's `LPAD` **truncates** when the target length is shorter than the input, so padding to 6 lost the high digits. DB2 pads to 10 (INTEGER width) then takes the last 6. Let me correct and re-verify.

CREATE VIEW V_CUSTOMER_INVOICES

CREATE VIEW V_INVOICE_DETAIL
COMMENT = '{ "origin": "sf_sc", "name": "snowconvert", "version": {  "major": 2,  "minor": 51,  "patch": "1-Pr" }, "attributes": {  "component": "db2",  "convertedOn": "11/11/2026",  "domain": "no-domain-provided",  "migrationid": "+8mhARM3jnqjj/PQbquepw==" }}'
AS
SELECT I.INVNO,
	      I.INVDATE,
	      I.INVCUST,
	      L.LINE_NO,
	      P.SKU,
	      P.PRODUCT_NAME,
	      L.QUANTITY,
	      L.UNIT_PRICE,
	      L.LINE_TOTAL
FROM
	INVOICES I

		INVOICE_LINES L ON L.INVNO = I.INVNO

CREATE VIEW V_MONTHLY_SALES
COMMENT = '{ "origin": "sf_sc", "name": "snowconvert", "version": {  "major": 2,  "minor": 51,  "patch": "1-Pr" }, "attributes": {  "component": "db2",  "convertedOn": "11/11/2026",  "domain": "no-domain-provided",  "migrationid": "+8mhARM3jnqjj/PQbquepw==" }}'
AS
SELECT
	YEAR(INVDATE) AS SALES_YEAR,
	MONTH(INVDATE) AS SALES_MONTH,
	COUNT(*) AS INVOICE_COUNT,
	SUM(INVTOTAL) AS TOTAL_SALES,
	AVG(INVTOTAL) AS AVG_INVOICE
FROM
	INVOICES
GROUP BY YEAR(INVDATE), MONTH(INVDATE);
CREATE VIEW V_PRODUCT_SALES
COMMENT = '{ "origin": "sf_sc", "name": "snowconvert", "version": {  "major": 2,  "minor": 51,  "patch": "1-Pr" }, "attributes": {  "component": "db2",  "convertedOn": "11/11/2026",  "domain": "no-domain-provided",  "migrationid": "+8mhARM3jnqjj/PQbquepw==" }}'
AS
SELECT P.SKU,
	      P.PRODUCT_NAME,
	      P.CATEGORY,
	COALESCE(SUM(L.QUANTITY), 0) AS UNITS_SOLD,
	COALESCE(SUM(L.LINE_TOTAL), 0) AS REVENUE
FROM
	PRODUCTS P
	    LEFT OUTER JOIN
		INVOICE_LINES L
	    ON L.PRODUCT_ID = P.PRODUCT_ID
GROUP BY P.SKU, P.PRODUCT_NAME, P.CATEGORY;
CREATE VIEW V_PROMO_USAGE
COMMENT = '{ "origin": "sf_sc", "name": "snowconvert", "version": {  "major": 2,  "minor": 51,  "patch": "1-Pr" }, "attributes": {  "component": "db2",  "convertedOn": "11/11/2026",  "domain": "no-domain-provided",  "migrationid": "+8mhARM3jnqjj/PQbquepw==" }}'

COMMENT = '{ "origin": "sf_sc", "name": "snowconvert", "version": {  "major": 2,  "minor": 51,  "patch": "1-Pr" }, "attributes": {  "component": "db2",  "convertedOn": "11/11/2026",  "domain": "no-domain-provided",  "migrationid": "+8mhARM3jnqjj/PQbquepw==" }}'
AS
SELECT I.WAREHOUSE_ID,
	      P.PRODUCT_ID,
	      P.SKU,
	      P.PRODUCT_NAME,
	      I.ON_HAND_QTY,
	      I.ALLOCATED_QTY,
	      (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) AS AVAILABLE_QTY,
	      I.REORDER_POINT,
	      I.REORDER_QTY,
	      I.SAFETY_STOCK,
	      I.BIN_LOCATION,

WHERE (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) <= I.REORDER_POINT;

CREATE VIEW V_INVOICE_DETAIL
COMMENT = '{ "origin": "sf_sc", "name": "snowconvert", "version": {  "major": 2,  "minor": 51,  "patch": "1-Pr" }, "attributes": {  "component": "db2",  "convertedOn": "11/11/2026",  "domain": "no-domain-provided",  "migrationid": "+8mhARM3jnqjj/PQbquepw==" }}'
AS
SELECT I.INVNO,
	      I.INVDATE,
	      I.INVCUST,
	      L.LINE_NO,
	      P.SKU,
	      P.PRODUCT_NAME,
	      L.QUANTITY,
	      L.UNIT_PRICE,
	      L.LINE_TOTAL
FROM

CREATE VIEW V_MONTHLY_SALES
COMMENT = '{ "origin": "sf_sc", "name": "snowconvert", "version": {  "major": 2,  "minor": 51,  "patch": "1-Pr" }, "attributes": {  "component": "db2",  "convertedOn": "11/11/2026",  "domain": "no-domain-provided",  "migrationid": "+8mhARM3jnqjj/PQbquepw==" }}'
AS
SELECT
	YEAR(INVDATE) AS SALES_YEAR,
	MONTH(INVDATE) AS SALES_MONTH,
	COUNT(*) AS INVOICE_COUNT,
	SUM(INVTOTAL) AS TOTAL_SALES,

CREATE VIEW V_ORDER_FULFILLMENT_STATUS
COMMENT = '{ "origin": "sf_sc", "name": "snowconvert", "version": {  "major": 2,  "minor": 51,  "patch": "1-Pr" }, "attributes": {  "component": "db2",  "convertedOn": "11/11/2026",  "domain": "no-domain-provided",  "migrationid": "+8mhARM3jnqjj/PQbquepw==" }}'
AS
SELECT O.ORDER_ID,

	RTRIM(C.FNAME) || ' ' || RTRIM(C.LNAME) AS CUSTOMER_NAME,
	      C.STATE,

	      O.REQUIRED_DATE,

CREATE VIEW V_INVENTORY_RESTOCK_ALERT
COMMENT = '{ "origin": "sf_sc", "name": "snowconvert", "version": {  "major": 2,  "minor": 51,  "patch": "1-Pr" }, "attributes": {  "component": "db2",  "convertedOn": "11/11/2026",  "domain": "no-domain-provided",  "migrationid": "+8mhARM3jnqjj/PQbquepw==" }}'
AS
SELECT I.WAREHOUSE_ID,
	      P.PRODUCT_ID,
	      P.SKU,
	      P.PRODUCT_NAME,
	      I.ON_HAND_QTY,
	      I.ALLOCATED_QTY,
	      (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) AS AVAILABLE_QTY,
	      I.REORDER_POINT,
	      I.REORDER_QTY,
	      I.SAFETY_STOCK,
	      I.BIN_LOCATION,
	      CASE
	        WHEN (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) <= I.SAFETY_STOCK THEN 'CRITICAL'
	        WHEN (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) <= I.REORDER_POINT THEN 'REORDER_NOW'
	        ELSE 'HEALTHY'
	      END AS INVENTORY_STATUS
FROM
	INVENTORY I
	    INNER JOIN
	        PRODUCTS P ON P.PRODUCT_ID = I.PRODUCT_ID
WHERE (I.ON_HAND_QTY - I.ALLOCATED_QTY) <= I.REORDER_POINT;

AS

	COALESCE(SUM(O.TOTAL_AMOUNT), 0.00) AS LIFETIME_ORDER_VALUE,

	        ORDERS O ON O.CUSTNO = C.CUSTNO

I'm also noticing other problems beyond parameter modes: the exception handler uses SET for assignment instead of Snowflake's `:=` syntax, and there's inconsistent mixing of the two assignment styles, plus a CASE block attempting to use SET-style assignments which isn't valid Snowflake scripting syntax.

Snowflake doesn't enforce primary key or unique constraints, so the duplicate-key exception handler keyed on SQLSTATE 23505 is actually dead code that can never trigger. More critically, in SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE the original DB2 "CONTINUE HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND" idiom was converted to catch SQLSTATE 42S02, but that error never fires when a FETCH goes past the cursor's end in Snowflake — meaning the WHILE loop variable never gets set and the loop runs forever. Given the scope of rewriting six procedures with cursor FOR loops, exception redesign, and OUT-to-return changes, I'm realizing this is too much careful work to safely do all at once. Rather than risk errors from rewriting everything in one giant pass, I think the more valuable move is to report the newly discovered severe bugs now and propose a plan for tackling the rest.

I decide to actually do the full rewrite since the user wants everything fixed and verified by deployment, working through the procedures as a set before deploying to a scratch environment. For each one I'm settling on specific conversions: SP_ADD_CUSTOMER's status OUT becomes an integer return, the inventory shortage and order placement procedures return OBJECTs for their multiple outputs, and the remaining three (refresh summary, restock inventory, update address) each collapse their single OUT parameter into an integer return.

I also note that SP_ADD_CUSTOMER's duplicate-key exception handling is effectively dead code in Snowflake since there's no primary key enforcement, so I'll need to add an explicit existence check to preserve the original intent, even though that changes behavior slightly.

I decide the right approach is an explicit EXISTS check returning -1, which I'll flag clearly to the user as a behavioral change rather than silently leaving broken dead code. I'm also planning to replace WHILE+NOT FOUND cursor loops with idiomatic FOR cursor loops, add an explicit customer-existence check in SP_PLACE_ORDER, and swap the old date arithmetic for DATEADD and CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() syntax. #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turn the SnowConvert DB2 output into a deployable Snowflake script.

Reads  snowflake/bigdata_clean.sql   (converter output, left untouched)
       snowflake/procedures_fixed.sql (hand-written procedures)
Writes snowflake/bigdata_deploy.sql

Changes, all mechanical:
  1. Strip !!!RESOLVE EWI!!! /*** ... ***/!!! markers (not valid SQL).
  2. Drop db2look's CONNECT TO <db> statement.
  3. CREATE SCHEMA ... AUTHORIZATION -> CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS.
  4. In ALTER TABLE statements, drop DB2-only clauses:
       ENFORCED, ENABLE QUERY OPTIMIZATION, ON DELETE ..., ON UPDATE ...
  5. Collapse "ADD\\n CONSTRAINT" to "ADD CONSTRAINT".
  6. Append ENABLE NOVALIDATE to CHECK constraints (required by Snowflake
     for ALTER TABLE ADD CHECK; still enforced for new writes).
  7. Replace the converted procedures with procedures_fixed.sql.
"""
import pathlib
import re
import sys

root = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
src = root / "snowflake" / "bigdata_clean.sql"
procs = root / "snowflake" / "procedures_fixed.sql"
dest = root / "snowflake" / "bigdata_deploy.sql"

text = src.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
stats = {}

# 1. EWI markers
text, stats["ewi_markers_removed"] = re.subn(
    r"!!!RESOLVE EWI!!!\s*/\*\*\*.*?\*\*\*/!!!", "", text, flags=re.S
)

# split the DDL from the procedures
m = re.search(r"^CREATE PROCEDURE", text, flags=re.M)
if not m:
    sys.exit("could not locate CREATE PROCEDURE boundary")
ddl = text[: m.start()]

# 2. CONNECT TO <db>
ddl, stats["connect_removed"] = re.subn(
    r"^CONNECT TO \w+\s*;\s*$", "", ddl, flags=re.M
)

# 3. CREATE SCHEMA
ddl, stats["schema_rewritten"] = re.subn(
    r'^CREATE SCHEMA\s+("?BIGDATA"?)\s+AUTHORIZATION\s+"?\w+"?\s*;',
    r"CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS \1;",
    ddl,
    flags=re.M,
)

DROP_PATTERNS = (
    re.compile(r"^\s*ENFORCED\s*;?\s*$", re.I),
    re.compile(r"^\s*ENABLE QUERY OPTIMIZATION\s*;?\s*$", re.I),
    re.compile(r"^\s*ON\s+(DELETE|UPDATE)\b.*$", re.I),
)

counters = {"enforced": 0, "enable_query_opt": 0, "referential_actions": 0, "check_novalidate": 0}


def clean_alter(block):
    """Strip DB2-only clauses from one ALTER TABLE statement."""
    is_check = re.search(r"\bCHECK\b", block, re.I) is not None
    kept = []
    for line in block.split("\n"):
        if DROP_PATTERNS[0].match(line):
            counters["enforced"] += 1
            continue
        if DROP_PATTERNS[1].match(line):
            counters["enable_query_opt"] += 1
            continue
        if DROP_PATTERNS[2].match(line):
            counters["referential_actions"] += 1
            continue
        kept.append(line)
    out = "\n".join(kept)
    out = re.sub(r"\bADD\s*\n\s*CONSTRAINT", "ADD CONSTRAINT", out)
    out = out.rstrip().rstrip(";").rstrip()
    if is_check:
        counters["check_novalidate"] += 1
        out += "\n  ENABLE NOVALIDATE;"
    else:
        out += ";"
    return out


# 4-6. walk statements, cleaning only ALTER TABLE ones
lines = ddl.split("\n")
result = []
buf = []
for line in lines:
    buf.append(line)
    if line.rstrip().endswith(";"):
        chunk = "\n".join(buf)
        idx = next(
            (i for i, l in enumerate(buf) if re.match(r"^\s*ALTER TABLE", l, re.I)), None
        )
        if idx is None:
            result.append(chunk)
        else:
            lead = "\n".join(buf[:idx])
            body = clean_alter("\n".join(buf[idx:]))
            result.append((lead + "\n" + body) if lead.strip() else body)
        buf = []
if buf:
    result.append("\n".join(buf))

ddl_out = "\n".join(result)
stats.update(counters)

# 7. procedures
proc_text = procs.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

header = (
    "-- Deployable Snowflake script generated from the SnowConvert DB2 output.\n"
    "-- Source: snowflake/bigdata_clean.sql (unmodified) + snowflake/procedures_fixed.sql\n"
    "-- NOTE: FOREIGN KEY and PRIMARY KEY constraints are metadata only in\n"
    "--       Snowflake and are NOT enforced. CHECK constraints ARE enforced.\n\n"
)

dest.write_text(header + ddl_out.rstrip() + "\n\n" + proc_text, encoding="utf-8")

print("wrote", dest)
for k, v in stats.items():
    print(f"  {k}: {v}")
remaining = len(re.findall(r"RESOLVE EWI|ENFORCED|ENABLE QUERY OPTIMIZATION", dest.read_text()))
print(f"  residual_db2_artifacts: {remaining}")

Reads  snowflake/bigdata_clean.sql   (converter output, left untouched)
       snowflake/procedures_fixed.sql (hand-written procedures)
Writes snowflake/bigdata_deploy.sql

Changes, all mechanical:
  1. Strip !!!RESOLVE EWI!!! /*** ... ***/!!! markers (not valid SQL).
  2. Drop db2look's CONNECT TO <db> statement.
  3. CREATE SCHEMA ... AUTHORIZATION -> CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS.
  4. In ALTER TABLE statements, drop DB2-only clauses:
       ENFORCED, ENABLE QUERY OPTIMIZATION, ON DELETE ..., ON UPDATE ...
  5. Collapse "ADD\\n CONSTRAINT" to "ADD CONSTRAINT".
  6. Append ENABLE NOVALIDATE to CHECK constraints (required by Snowflake
     for ALTER TABLE ADD CHECK; still enforced for new writes).
  7. Replace the converted procedures with procedures_fixed.sql.
"""
import pathlib
import re
import sys

root = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
src = root / "snowflake" / "bigdata_clean.sql"
procs = root / "snowflake" / "procedures_fixed.sql"
dest = root / "snowflake" / "bigdata_deploy.sql"

text = src.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
stats = {}

# 1. EWI markers
text, stats["ewi_markers_removed"] = re.subn(
    r"!!!RESOLVE EWI!!!\s*/\*\*\*.*?\*\*\*/!!!", "", text, flags=re.S
)

# split the DDL from the procedures
m = re.search(r"^CREATE PROCEDURE", text, flags=re.M)
if not m:
    sys.exit("could not locate CREATE PROCEDURE boundary")
ddl = text[: m.start()]

# 2. CONNECT TO <db>
ddl, stats["connect_removed"] = re.subn(
    r"^CONNECT TO \w+\s*;\s*$", "", ddl, flags=re.M
)

# 3. CREATE SCHEMA
ddl, stats["schema_rewritten"] = re.subn(
    r'^CREATE SCHEMA\s+("?BIGDATA"?)\s+AUTHORIZATION\s+"?\w+"?\s*;',
    r"CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS \1;",
    ddl,
    flags=re.M,
)

DROP_PATTERNS = (
    re.compile(r"^\s*ENFORCED\s*;?\s*$", re.I),
    re.compile(r"^\s*ENABLE QUERY OPTIMIZATION\s*;?\s*$", re.I),
    re.compile(r"^\s*ON\s+(DELETE|UPDATE)\b.*$", re.I),
)

counters = {"enforced": 0, "enable_query_opt": 0, "referential_actions": 0, "check_novalidate": 0}

    """Strip DB2-only clauses from one ALTER TABLE statement."""
    is_check = re.search(r"\bCHECK\b", block, re.I) is not None
    kept = []
    for line in block.split("\n"):
        if DROP_PATTERNS[0].match(line):
            counters["enforced"] += 1
            continue
        if DROP_PATTERNS[1].match(line):
            counters["enable_query_opt"] += 1
            continue
        if DROP_PATTERNS[2].match(line):
            counters["referential_actions"] += 1
            continue

    out = "\n".join(kept)
    out = re.sub(r"\bADD\s*\n\s*CONSTRAINT", "ADD CONSTRAINT", out)
    out = out.rstrip().rstrip(";").rstrip()

        counters["check_novalidate"] += 1
        out += "\n  ENABLE NOVALIDATE;"
    else:
        out += ";"
    return out


# 4-6. walk statements, cleaning only ALTER TABLE ones
lines = ddl.split("\n")
result = []
buf = []
for line in lines:
    buf.append(line)
    if line.rstrip().endswith(";"):
        chunk = "\n".join(buf)
        idx = next(
            (i for i, l in enumerate(buf) if re.match(r"^\s*ALTER TABLE", l, re.I)), None
        )

            result.append(chunk)
        else:
            lead = "\n".join(buf[:idx])
            body = clean_alter("\n".join(buf[idx:]))
            result.append((lead + "\n" + body) if lead.strip() else body)
        buf = []
if buf:
    result.append("\n".join(buf))

ddl_out = "\n".join(result)
stats.update(counters)

# 7. procedures
proc_text = procs.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

header = (
    "-- Deployable Snowflake script generated from the SnowConvert DB2 output.\n"
    "-- Source: snowflake/bigdata_clean.sql (unmodified) + snowflake/procedures_fixed.sql\n"
    "-- NOTE: FOREIGN KEY and PRIMARY KEY constraints are metadata only in\n"
    "--       Snowflake and are NOT enforced. CHECK constraints ARE enforced.\n\n"
)

dest.write_text(header + ddl_out.rstrip() + "\n\n" + proc_text, encoding="utf-8")

print("wrote", dest)
for k, v in stats.items():
    print(f"  {k}: {v}")
remaining = len(re.findall(r"RESOLVE EWI|ENFORCED|ENABLE QUERY OPTIMIZATION", dest.read_text()))
print(f"  residual_db2_artifacts: {remaining}")

Reads  snowflake/bigdata_clean.sql   (converter output, left untouched)

       ENFORCED, ENABLE QUERY OPTIMIZATION, ON DELETE ..., ON UPDATE ...
  5. Collapse "ADD\\n CONSTRAINT" to "ADD CONSTRAINT".
  6. Append ENABLE NOVALIDATE to CHECK constraints (required by Snowflake
     for ALTER TABLE ADD CHECK; still enforced for new writes).
  7. Replace the converted procedures with procedures_fixed.sql.
"""
import pathlib
import re
import sys

src = root / "snowflake" / "bigdata_clean.sql"
procs = root / "snowflake" / "procedures_fixed.sql"
dest = root / "snowflake" / "bigdata_deploy.sql"

text = src.read_text(encoding="utf-8-sig")
stats = {}

# 1. EWI markers
text, stats["ewi_markers_removed"] = re.subn(
    r"!!!RESOLVE EWI!!!\s*/\*\*\*.*?\*\*\*/!!!", "", text, flags=re.S
)

# split the DDL from the procedures
m = re.search(r"^CREATE PROCEDURE", text, flags=re.M)
if not m:
    sys.exit("could not locate CREATE PROCEDURE boundary")
ddl = text[: m.start()]

# 2. CONNECT TO <db>
ddl, stats["connect_removed"] = re.subn(
    r"^CONNECT TO \w+\s*;\s*$", "", ddl, flags=re.M
)

# 3. CREATE SCHEMA
ddl, stats["schema_rewritten"] = re.subn(
    r'^CREATE SCHEMA\s+("?BIGDATA"?)\s+AUTHORIZATION\s+"?\w+"?\s*;',
    r"CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS \1;",
    ddl,
    flags=re.M,
)

# 3b. IDENTITY(+1000, +1) -> IDENTITY(1000, 1).
# SnowConvert carries DB2's signed START WITH / INCREMENT BY through verbatim;
# Snowflake rejects the leading '+'. No EWI is emitted for this.
ddl, stats["identity_signs_fixed"] = re.subn(
    r"IDENTITY\(\s*\+?(-?\d+)\s*,\s*\+?(-?\d+)\s*\)",
    r"IDENTITY(\1, \2)",

)

    re.compile(r"^\s*ENFORCED\s*;?\s*$", re.I),
    re.compile(r"^\s*ENABLE QUERY OPTIMIZATION\s*;?\s*$", re.I),
    re.compile(r"^\s*ON\s+(DELETE|UPDATE)\b.*$", re.I),
)

            counters["enforced"] += 1
            continue

            counters["enable_query_opt"] += 1
            continue
        if DROP_PATTERNS[2].match(line):
            counters["referential_actions"] += 1
            continue
        kept.append(line)
    out = "\n".join(kept)
    out = re.sub(r"\bADD\s*\n\s*CONSTRAINT", "ADD CONSTRAINT", out)
    out = out.rstrip().rstrip(";").rstrip()
    if is_check:
        counters["check_novalidate"] += 1
        out += "\n  ENABLE NOVALIDATE;"
    else:
        out += ";"
    return out

messages.text:
Everything's clean, so now I'll put together the final summary covering the full deployment: all 30 objects migrated to DB2_MIGRATION_SCRATCH.BIGDATA with zero errors, functional tests passing, 11 CHECK constraints enforced, and FKs captured as metadata only.

The deliverables include the deployable SQL script, hand-written procedures, the cleaned converter output with preserved fixes, the original pristine DB2 DDL, and the transformation script. I also want to document the converter's defects I found worth flagging — things like parse errors from the db2look preamble, invalid EWI markers, bad parameter modes, pass-through of invalid constructs like GET DIAGNOSTICS and CONDITION/SIGNAL, nonexistent functions, missing EWI warnings on IDENTITY syntax, and a silent logic bug where NOT FOUND handlers get mistranslated. I should also note the three corrections I made myself during the session regarding false claims about criticals, CHECK support, and the LPAD width bug.

There's still open items remaining: the 15 unenforced foreign keys as a design decision, the fact that git has no commits or remote yet, data migration still pending, and that deployment only happened to scratch rather than a real target. I want to lay out next-step options — deploying to a real database, migrating data, committing to git, or revisiting FK strategy — and ask which direction to take, keeping the writeup organized without overloading it.

Everything verified and test rows removed. Here's where the migration stands.

## Deployment verified end to end

All 30 objects deployed to `DB2_MIGRATION_SCRATCH.BIGDATA` with **zero errors**: 1 schema, 2 sequences, 11 tables, 8 views, 3 functions, 6 procedures.

**Functional results, compared against DB2 where applicable:**

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `FN_FORMAT_INVNO(62358)` | `062358` — matches DB2 |
| `FN_FORMAT_INVNO(1234567)` | `234567` — matches DB2 |
| `FN_INVOICE_TOTAL(100,15,6)` | `121.00` |
| `FN_CUSTOMER_FULLNAME('Ada  ','Lovelace ')` | `Ada Lovelace` — trailing blanks trimmed |
| `SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE()` | `{0, 0}` — **returned instead of looping forever** |
| `SP_ADD_CUSTOMER` new / duplicate | `0` then `-1` — **duplicate path now actually reachable** |
| `SP_UPDATE_CUSTOMER_ADDRESS` | `1` — `SQLROWCOUNT` works |
| `SP_PLACE_ORDER` | `{order_id: 5000, total: 227}` — 200 + 12 TX tax + 15 freight, tax tiering correct |
| `SP_PLACE_ORDER` unknown customer | raises `CUST_MISSING: Customer does not exist…` — **the mistranslated handler now fires** |
| `SP_RESTOCK_INVENTORY` unknown item | raises `INV_NOT_FOUND` |
| `PROMOTIONS.DISCOUNT_PCT = 250` | **rejected** — check constraint enforced |

## Converter defects found

Eleven distinct problems, of which **only four carried any warning at the right severity**:

| Defect | Warning given? |
|---|---|
| `IN`/`OUT` parameter modes emitted — invalid syntax | Yes, but as "Medium / pending review" |
| `GET DIAGNOSTICS` passed through | Yes, Medium |
| `CONDITION` + `SIGNAL` passed through | Yes, Medium |
| `DAYS()` / `DIGITS()` — functions that don't exist | Yes, Medium |
| `!!!RESOLVE EWI!!!` markers are not valid SQL | No |
| `IDENTITY(+1000, +1)` — `+` rejected | **No warning at all** |
| `ALTER COLUMN ... RESTART WITH` | Yes, Medium |
| `ENFORCED` / `ENABLE QUERY OPTIMIZATION` retained | Partly, as FDM |
| `NOT FOUND` handler remapped to `42S02` | **No — silent logic bug** |
| `SSC-EWI-0035` claims `CHECK` unsupported | **Wrong — it is supported and enforced** |
| 56 parse errors from `db2look` preamble | Yes, Critical |

I also corrected myself three times: claiming no critical issues, claiming Snowflake lacks `CHECK` support, and a bad `LPAD` width that DB2 comparison caught.

## Files

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `snowflake/bigdata_deploy.sql` | **Deployable** — 906 lines, verified |
| `snowflake/procedures_fixed.sql` | Hand-rewritten procedures |
| `snowflake/bigdata_clean.sql` | Converter output, preserved |
| `db2_ddl/bigdata.sql` | Pristine `db2look` original |
| `make_deployable.py` | The transform, re-runnable |

## Still open

- **15 foreign keys are not enforced.** Confirmed by inserting an orphan row successfully. This is a real design gap, unaddressed.
- **Deployed to scratch, not a real target.** `DB2_MIGRATION_SCRATCH.BIGDATA` is a verification sandbox.
- **No data migrated.** All tables are empty; DB2 has no automated data migration here.
- **Git: nothing committed since the first conversion, and still no remote.** This is now a substantial body of verified work sitting on one machine.

messages.text:
I'm now laying out the foreign key gap analysis, separating the nine FKs into risk classes—starting with the two CASCADE deletes that were lost, which create silent orphaned-row corruption since Snowflake no longer propagates deletes from parent to child tables the way DB2 did.

The second class covers the seven NO ACTION constraints that previously blocked orphan inserts; mapping each one to whether any existing procedure actually enforces that check reveals most tables have zero coverage, with SP_PLACE_ORDER validating customer existence and SP_RESTOCK only partially checking inventory rather than the products table itself. This leaves several tables—INVOICES, INVOICE_LINES, ORDER_ITEMS, PRODUCTS—with no procedural writes enforcing referential integrity at all.

I'm weighing remediation options: scheduled integrity checks to detect orphans after the fact, strengthening procedures (limited since most parent tables are externally written), replacing CASCADE deletes with explicit delete procedures to restore proper cascade semantics, or simply documenting the accepted risk.

The most honest approach is combining explicit delete procedures for the two cascade relationships with scheduled detection across all nine, since procedure-level enforcement alone won't reach far enough. I should lay out these options concisely and ask what they'd like me to implement.

## The foreign key gap, assessed

Nine foreign keys, in two risk classes.

**Class 1 — lost `CASCADE` deletes (2). This is the serious one.**

| Constraint | Child → Parent | DB2 | Snowflake now |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LINES_INV_FK` | `INVOICE_LINES` → `INVOICES` | deleting an invoice deletes its lines | **lines orphaned, silently** |
| `ITEMS_ORDER_FK` | `ORDER_ITEMS` → `ORDERS` | deleting an order deletes its items | **items orphaned, silently** |

These are dangerous precisely because nothing errors. Existing `DELETE` code keeps working and quietly changes meaning — proven above with `D = 1`.

**Class 2 — lost orphan prevention (7).**

| Constraint | Child column → Parent | Protected by procedure logic? |
|---|---|---|
| `ORDERS_CUST_FK` | `ORDERS.CUSTNO` → `CUSTOMERS` | **Yes** — `SP_PLACE_ORDER` checks |
| `TXN_PROD_FK` | `INVENTORY_TRANSACTIONS.PRODUCT_ID` → `PRODUCTS` | Partly — checks `INVENTORY`, not `PRODUCTS` |
| `INV_CUST_FK` | `INVOICES.INVCUST` → `CUSTOMERS` | No |
| `INV_PROM_FK` | `INVOICES.INVPROM` → `PROMOTIONS` | No — proven, `NOPROMO` accepted |
| `LINES_PROD_FK` | `INVOICE_LINES.PRODUCT_ID` → `PRODUCTS` | No |
| `ITEMS_PROD_FK` | `ORDER_ITEMS.PRODUCT_ID` → `PRODUCTS` | No |
| `INV_PROD_FK` | `INVENTORY.PRODUCT_ID` → `PRODUCTS` | No |

Critically, **`INVOICES`, `INVOICE_LINES`, `ORDER_ITEMS`, `PRODUCTS` and `PROMOTIONS` are not written by any procedure.** Whatever loads them — ETL, application, bulk load — is the only possible enforcement point. So procedure-level validation cannot cover most of this; only one of nine is genuinely covered today.

One mitigating factor worth stating: if these tables are only ever loaded from DB2, where the constraints *were* enforced, the migrated data arrives already consistent. The exposure is ongoing writes and deletes after cutover, not the initial load.

**(b) More importantly, the one procedure that does move data between tables won't generate lineage even when it runs.** `SP_REFRESH_CUSTOMER_SUMMARY` reads `INVOICES` and writes `CUSTOMER_SALES_SUMMARY`, but row-by-row out of a cursor:

```sql
FOR R IN C1 DO
  INSERT INTO CUSTOMER_SALES_SUMMARY (...) VALUES (R.INVCUST, R.CNT, ...);
```

The values arrive as script variables, so Snowflake can't attribute them back to `INVOICES` columns. I wrote it that way because it was faithful to your DB2 cursor loop — but a set-based `INSERT … SELECT` would produce identical results, run far faster, **and** create the real `INVOICES → CUSTOMER_SALES_SUMMARY` lineage edge.

And to be explicit: **foreign keys never appear in lineage.** Lineage is not an ER diagram. All 9 of your FKs are registered in Snowflake — I just confirmed all nine by name — and they contribute nothing to that graph.

One caveat on my own certainty: my role is `SYSADMIN`, which can't read `SNOWFLAKE.ACCOUNT_USAGE.OBJECT_DEPENDENCIES` or `ACCESS_HISTORY`, so I couldn't inspect the graph server-side to confirm. This comes from the DDL and Snowflake's lineage model. Also worth noting your screenshot shows **`Filters 1`** active, which may itself be hiding node types.

Still outstanding are the 7 accepted-risk foreign keys, no data migrated, and the deployment currently living only in the sandbox I picked without asking. The code is sound and worth committing; I just don't want "commit" to imply the migration is finished.

# DB2 → Snowflake Migration: `BIGDATA` schema

Migration of the `BIGDATA` schema from IBM DB2 to Snowflake, carried out with
Snowflake AIM for Data Warehouses (SnowConvert 2.51.1-Pr) plus manual repair of
the converted code.

**Status: converted, repaired, deployed and functionally verified in a sandbox
database. No data has been migrated.** See [Open items](#open-items).

---

## Source

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | IBM DB2 / Linux x86-64, version 12.1.5.0 |
| Host | Docker container `mydb2` (`icr.io/db2_community/db2`), `localhost:50000` |
| Database | `testdb` |
| Schema | `BIGDATA` (the `SALES_DEMO` schema was explicitly out of scope) |

30 objects: 1 schema, 2 sequences, 11 tables, 8 views, 3 functions, 6 procedures.
No triggers. All routines are `LANGUAGE SQL` (no embedded C or Java).

Constraints in the source: **11 primary keys, 11 check constraints, 9 foreign keys.**

## Target

| | |
|---|---|
| Account | `QAQGBZD-SNOWCONVERT_AI_POC` |
| Connection | `db2_aim_key` (key-pair auth, role `SYSADMIN`) |
| Database / schema | `DB2_MIGRATION_SCRATCH.BIGDATA` |
| Warehouse | `MIGRATION_WH` |

> `DB2_MIGRATION_SCRATCH` was originally chosen as a verification sandbox and
> then retained as the deployment target by decision. It is **not** a
> production target.

---

## Important: DB2 is a conversion-only source in AIM

The tooling supports the full migration lifecycle only for SqlServer, Redshift,
Teradata, Postgresql, Oracle, BigQuery and AzureSynapse. For DB2 the following
are **not available**, each confirmed by running the command:

| Capability | Result |
|---|---|
| `scai code extract` (pull DDL from the live database) | `EXT0003: Code extraction is not supported for this source language` |
| `scai code deploy` | `DEP0008: Code deployment is not supported for source language 'Db2'` |
| Code Unit Registry | Never generated — DB2 has no arrange phase |
| `scai assessment waves` / `object-exclusion` / `data-lineage` | `ASM0011` / `ASM0026` / `ASM0035` — all require the registry |
| Orchestrated data migration / validation | Unavailable |
| `query_source` ad-hoc SQL | `QRY0006` — connection test only |

Consequences: there is **no per-object tracking, no dependency waves and no
`multi_report.html`** for this project, and deployment was done manually. DDL
was produced with `db2look` inside the container, not by `scai code extract`.

---

## Pipeline actually used

```
db2look (in container)        ->  db2_ddl/bigdata.sql          pristine DB2 DDL
filter db2look scaffolding    ->  db2_ddl/bigdata_clean.sql    input to conversion
scai code add + convert       ->  snowflake/bigdata_clean.sql  SnowConvert output
make_deployable.py            ->  snowflake/bigdata_deploy.sql deployable script
manual rewrite                ->  snowflake/procedures_fixed.sql
new work                      ->  snowflake/cascade_procedures.sql
```

## Files

| Path | Description |
|---|---|
| `db2_ddl/bigdata.sql` | Pristine `db2look` output. Never edited. |
| `db2_ddl/bigdata_clean.sql` | Same, minus `db2look` session scaffolding (see below). |
| `source/bigdata_clean.sql` | Conversion input as registered in the project. |
| `snowflake/bigdata_clean.sql` | Raw SnowConvert output (plus the `DAYS`/`DIGITS` fixes). **Not deployable.** |
| `snowflake/bigdata_deploy.sql` | **The deployable script.** Verified against Snowflake. |
| `snowflake/procedures_fixed.sql` | The 6 procedures, hand-rewritten. Embedded in the deploy script. |
| `snowflake/cascade_procedures.sql` | `SP_DELETE_INVOICE`, `SP_DELETE_ORDER` — new, replace lost `ON DELETE CASCADE`. Deployed separately. |
| `make_deployable.py` | Re-runnable transform: `bigdata_clean.sql` + `procedures_fixed.sql` → `bigdata_deploy.sql`. |
| `.scai/reports/SnowConvert/` | Conversion reports, incl. `Issues.*.csv` and `AssessmentReport.*.docx`. |

### Reproducing

```bash
python3 make_deployable.py
{ echo "USE WAREHOUSE MIGRATION_WH;"; \
  echo "USE DATABASE DB2_MIGRATION_SCRATCH;"; \
  cat snowflake/bigdata_deploy.sql; } | snow sql -c db2_aim_key -i

{ echo "USE SCHEMA DB2_MIGRATION_SCRATCH.BIGDATA;"; \
  cat snowflake/cascade_procedures.sql; } | snow sql -c db2_aim_key -i
```

`bigdata_deploy.sql` uses bare `CREATE` (not `CREATE OR REPLACE`) for tables, so
re-running against a populated schema fails with `42710 object already exists`.
Drop the schema first for a clean redeploy.

---

## Problems found in the converted output

SnowConvert's JSON envelope reported `76 issues` with `ewi.bySeverity:
{medium: 1, low: 2}` and **no critical count**. The `Issues` CSV for the same run
contained **132 rows, 56 of them Critical**. The envelope's EWI tally excludes
parse errors — do not treat it as a measure of correctness.

Eleven distinct defects, of which four carried a usefully-severe warning:

| # | Defect | Warned? | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 56 parse errors from `db2look`'s repeated `SET SYSIBM.NLS_STRING_UNITS` / `SET CURRENT SCHEMA` / `SET CURRENT PATH` preamble | Critical | Filtered from the input (54 lines) before conversion |
| 2 | `!!!RESOLVE EWI!!! /*** … ***/!!!` markers are **not valid SQL** (bare `!!!`) | No | 50 stripped by `make_deployable.py` |
| 3 | `IN` / `OUT` parameter modes emitted; Snowflake has no parameter modes | Only as "Medium / pending review" | Procedures rewritten; `OUT` params became return values |
| 4 | `GET DIAGNOSTICS … = ROW_COUNT` passed through | Medium | `V_ROWS := SQLROWCOUNT` |
| 5 | `DECLARE … CONDITION FOR SQLSTATE` + `SIGNAL` passed through | Medium | `DECLARE … EXCEPTION (…)` + `RAISE` |
| 6 | `DAYS()` and `DIGITS()` emitted — neither function exists in Snowflake | Medium | `DATEDIFF`; `RIGHT(LPAD(TO_VARCHAR(ABS(x)),10,'0'),6)` |
| 7 | `IDENTITY(+1000, +1)` — Snowflake rejects the `+` | **No warning at all** | 6 occurrences de-signed |
| 8 | `ALTER COLUMN … RESTART WITH 6000` has no Snowflake equivalent | Medium | Folded into the column's `IDENTITY` start value |
| 9 | `ENFORCED` (35) and `ENABLE QUERY OPTIMIZATION` (11) retained | Partly, as FDM | Removed |
| 10 | `SSC-EWI-0035 "CHECK STATEMENT NOT SUPPORTED"` | — | **The EWI is wrong.** See below. |
| 11 | `EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND` remapped to `SQLSTATE '42S02'` | **No — silent logic bug** | Restored intent explicitly |

### Defect 10: `CHECK` constraints *are* supported

Snowflake supports and **enforces** `CHECK` constraints. Verified: inserting
`DISCOUNT_PCT = 250` into `PROMOTIONS` is rejected. All 11 check constraints were
preserved, not dropped.

`ALTER TABLE … ADD CONSTRAINT … CHECK` requires `ENABLE NOVALIDATE`
(`ALTER TABLE ADD CHECK is not supported with ENABLE VALIDATE`). This skips
validation of pre-existing rows but **still enforces new writes** — verified.

### Defect 11: the silent handler bug

DB2 source:

```sql
DECLARE EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND          -- SQLSTATE 02000, "no rows found"
  SIGNAL CUST_MISSING SET MESSAGE_TEXT = 'Customer does not exist …';
```

SnowConvert output:

```sql
WHEN OTHER EXIT THEN
  CASE WHEN (SQLSTATE = '42S02') THEN      -- "base table or view not found"
```

`42S02` is a different condition. The handler would have fired only if the
`CUSTOMERS` table were missing, and **never** when a customer did not exist —
the only case it was written for. Had the syntax errors not blocked deployment,
`SP_PLACE_ORDER` would silently have accepted orders for non-existent customers.

A second instance of the same class: `SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE` used DB2's
`CONTINUE HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND SET V_AT_END = 1` cursor-exhaustion idiom,
remapped to `42S02`, so `V_AT_END` never became 1 — **an infinite `WHILE` loop.**
Both were replaced with cursor `FOR` loops, which terminate by construction.

---

## Procedure changes

Snowflake procedures take input-only parameters and return a single value, so
every `OUT` parameter became part of the return. **This is a breaking interface
change for callers.**

| Procedure | DB2 `OUT` params | Snowflake signature |
|---|---|---|
| `SP_ADD_CUSTOMER` | `P_STATUS` | `RETURNS INTEGER` |
| `SP_REFRESH_CUSTOMER_SUMMARY` | `P_ROWS` | `RETURNS INTEGER` |
| `SP_UPDATE_CUSTOMER_ADDRESS` | `P_ROWS` | `RETURNS INTEGER` |
| `SP_RESTOCK_INVENTORY` | `P_NEW_ON_HAND` | `RETURNS INTEGER` |
| `SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE` | count + deficit | `RETURNS OBJECT` |
| `SP_PLACE_ORDER` | order id + total | `RETURNS OBJECT` |

One deliberate behaviour change: `SP_ADD_CUSTOMER` handled `SQLSTATE 23505`
(unique violation) to return `-1`. Snowflake does not enforce primary keys, so
that handler could never fire. The duplicate check is now an explicit
`COUNT(*)` probe, preserving the original intent.

---

## Constraint semantics in Snowflake

Each row below was verified by execution, not assumed.

| Constraint | Count | Declared | Enforced |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CHECK` | 11 | Yes | **Yes** |
| `NOT NULL` | — | Yes | Yes |
| `PRIMARY KEY` | 11 | Yes (metadata) | **No** |
| `FOREIGN KEY` | 9 | Yes (metadata) | **No** |

All 9 foreign keys are registered and visible via `SHOW IMPORTED KEYS`, but
Snowflake does not act on them. An orphan child row inserted against an empty
parent was accepted.

### Lost `ON DELETE CASCADE` — mitigated

| DB2 constraint | Behaviour lost |
|---|---|
| `LINES_INV_FK` | deleting an `INVOICES` row no longer deletes its `INVOICE_LINES` |
| `ITEMS_ORDER_FK` | deleting an `ORDERS` row no longer deletes its `ORDER_ITEMS` |

Replaced by `SP_DELETE_INVOICE(invno)` and `SP_DELETE_ORDER(order_id)`, which
delete children then parent in one transaction, rolling back and re-raising on
error.

> **These only help if callers use them.** A plain `DELETE FROM INVOICES` still
> orphans children silently. Any application or ETL code that deletes invoices
> or orders must be redirected to these procedures.

### Unenforced orphan prevention — risk accepted

| Constraint | Relationship | Covered by procedure logic? |
|---|---|---|
| `ORDERS_CUST_FK` | `ORDERS.CUSTNO` → `CUSTOMERS` | Yes — `SP_PLACE_ORDER` checks |
| `TXN_PROD_FK` | `INVENTORY_TRANSACTIONS.PRODUCT_ID` → `PRODUCTS` | Partly — checks `INVENTORY`, not `PRODUCTS` |
| `INV_CUST_FK` | `INVOICES.INVCUST` → `CUSTOMERS` | No |
| `INV_PROM_FK` | `INVOICES.INVPROM` → `PROMOTIONS` | No |
| `LINES_PROD_FK` | `INVOICE_LINES.PRODUCT_ID` → `PRODUCTS` | No |
| `ITEMS_PROD_FK` | `ORDER_ITEMS.PRODUCT_ID` → `PRODUCTS` | No |
| `INV_PROD_FK` | `INVENTORY.PRODUCT_ID` → `PRODUCTS` | No |

`INVOICES`, `INVOICE_LINES`, `ORDER_ITEMS`, `PRODUCTS` and `PROMOTIONS` are not
written by any procedure, so there is no interception point for them at all —
enforcement must live in whatever loads those tables. Initial migrated data
arrives already consistent (DB2 enforced these); the exposure is post-cutover
writes.

---

## Verification

Deployed with zero errors: 1 schema, 2 sequences, 11 tables, 8 views,
3 functions, 8 procedures (6 migrated + 2 new).

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `FN_FORMAT_INVNO(62358)` | `062358` — matches DB2 |
| `FN_FORMAT_INVNO(1234567)` | `234567` — matches DB2 |
| `FN_INVOICE_TOTAL(100,15,6)` | `121.00` |
| `FN_CUSTOMER_FULLNAME('Ada  ','Lovelace ')` | `Ada Lovelace` |
| `SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE()` | `{0, 0}` — returns, does not hang |
| `SP_ADD_CUSTOMER` new / duplicate | `0` then `-1` |
| `SP_UPDATE_CUSTOMER_ADDRESS` | `1` (`SQLROWCOUNT` works) |
| `SP_PLACE_ORDER` | `{order_id: 5000, total_amount: 227}` = 200 + 12 TX tax + 15 freight |
| `SP_PLACE_ORDER` unknown customer | raises `CUST_MISSING` |
| `SP_RESTOCK_INVENTORY` unknown item | raises `INV_NOT_FOUND` |
| `PROMOTIONS.DISCOUNT_PCT = 250` | rejected by check constraint |
| `SP_DELETE_INVOICE` | 1 invoice + 2 lines → 0 / 0 |
| `SP_DELETE_ORDER` | 1 order + 2 items → 0 / 0 |

`FN_FORMAT_INVNO` was validated against DB2's own output for `62358`, `1234567`,
`5`, `-42` and `0`. A first attempt using `LPAD(…, 6, '0')` returned `123456`
where DB2 returns `234567`: Snowflake's `LPAD` **truncates** when the target
length is shorter than the input. DB2's `DIGITS` pads an `INTEGER` to 10
characters, so the correct form pads to 10 and then takes the right 6.

All test rows were removed; every table is empty.

---

## Open items

1. **No data migrated.** All tables are empty. DB2 has no orchestrated data
   migration here, so this must be done manually (e.g. `db2 export` →
   `PUT` → `COPY INTO`) with row-count and checksum verification per table.
2. **7 foreign keys unenforced**, risk accepted. Revisit if post-cutover writes
   come from anywhere other than a trusted load process.
3. **Cascade deletes depend on callers** using `SP_DELETE_INVOICE` /
   `SP_DELETE_ORDER`.
4. **`OUT` → return value is a breaking change** for every existing caller of
   the six procedures.
5. **Deployed to `DB2_MIGRATION_SCRATCH`**, retained as target by decision.
6. **No table-to-table lineage.** Snowflake lineage is built from data movement,
   not relationships; foreign keys never appear in it. The tables are empty, and
   `SP_REFRESH_CUSTOMER_SUMMARY` writes row-by-row from a cursor
   (`INSERT … VALUES (R.col, …)`), so Snowflake cannot attribute values back to
   `INVOICES` columns. A set-based `INSERT … SELECT` would be faster and would
   produce the lineage edge; the cursor form was retained deliberately as a
   faithful translation of the DB2 logic.
7. **No assessment report** — unavailable for DB2 (see above).

# DB2 → Snowflake Migration: `BIGDATA` schema

Migration of the `BIGDATA` schema from IBM DB2 to Snowflake using Snowflake AIM
for Data Warehouses (SnowConvert 2.51.1-Pr), plus manual repair of the converted
code.

**Status: converted, repaired, deployed and functionally verified. No data has
been migrated.**

## Source and target

| | |
|---|---|
| Source | IBM DB2 12.1.5.0, Docker container `mydb2`, database `testdb`, schema `BIGDATA` |
| Target | Snowflake `DB2_MIGRATION_SCRATCH.BIGDATA` (account `QAQGBZD-SNOWCONVERT_AI_POC`, connection `db2_aim_key`, warehouse `MIGRATION_WH`) |

30 objects: 1 schema, 2 sequences, 11 tables, 8 views, 3 functions, 6 procedures.
No triggers; all routines are `LANGUAGE SQL`. Constraints: 11 primary keys,
11 check constraints, 9 foreign keys. `SALES_DEMO` was out of scope.

`DB2_MIGRATION_SCRATCH` began as a verification sandbox and was retained as the
target by decision. It is not a production target.

## DB2 is a conversion-only source in AIM

The full lifecycle is supported only for SqlServer, Redshift, Teradata,
Postgresql, Oracle, BigQuery and AzureSynapse. For DB2, each of these was tried
and failed:

| Capability | Result |
|---|---|
| `scai code extract` | `EXT0003: Code extraction is not supported for this source language` |
| `scai code deploy` | `DEP0008: Code deployment is not supported for source language 'Db2'` |
| Code Unit Registry | Never generated (no arrange phase for DB2) |
| `scai assessment waves` / `object-exclusion` / `data-lineage` | `ASM0011` / `ASM0026` / `ASM0035` — all need the registry |
| `query_source` ad-hoc SQL | `QRY0006` — connection test only |

So there is **no per-object tracking, no dependency waves and no assessment
report**. DDL came from `db2look` inside the container, and deployment was
manual via `snow sql`.

## Files

| Path | Description |
|---|---|
| `db2_ddl/bigdata.sql` | Pristine `db2look` output. Never edited. |
| `db2_ddl/bigdata_clean.sql` | Same, minus `db2look` session scaffolding. |
| `source/bigdata_clean.sql` | Conversion input as registered. |
| `snowflake/bigdata_clean.sql` | Raw SnowConvert output. **Not deployable.** |
| `snowflake/bigdata_deploy.sql` | **The deployable script.** Verified. |
| `snowflake/procedures_fixed.sql` | The 6 procedures, hand-rewritten. |
| `snowflake/cascade_procedures.sql` | `SP_DELETE_INVOICE`, `SP_DELETE_ORDER` — new. |
| `make_deployable.py` | Re-runnable transform producing `bigdata_deploy.sql`. |
| `.scai/reports/SnowConvert/` | Conversion reports, incl. `Issues.*.csv`. |

### Redeploy

```bash
python3 make_deployable.py
{ echo "USE WAREHOUSE MIGRATION_WH;"; echo "USE DATABASE DB2_MIGRATION_SCRATCH;"; \
  cat snowflake/bigdata_deploy.sql; } | snow sql -c db2_aim_key -i
{ echo "USE SCHEMA DB2_MIGRATION_SCRATCH.BIGDATA;"; \
  cat snowflake/cascade_procedures.sql; } | snow sql -c db2_aim_key -i
```

Tables use bare `CREATE`, so re-running against a populated schema fails with
`42710`. Drop the schema first for a clean redeploy.

## Defects found in the converted output

SnowConvert's JSON envelope reported `76 issues`, severities `{medium: 1,
low: 2}`, **no critical count**. The `Issues` CSV for the same run had **132
rows, 56 Critical**. The envelope excludes parse errors — do not use it to judge
correctness.

| # | Defect | Warned? | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 56 parse errors from `db2look`'s repeated `SET SYSIBM.NLS_STRING_UNITS` / `SET CURRENT SCHEMA` / `SET CURRENT PATH` | Critical | 54 lines filtered from input |
| 2 | `!!!RESOLVE EWI!!!` markers are **not valid SQL** | No | 50 stripped |
| 3 | `IN`/`OUT` parameter modes emitted; Snowflake has none | Only "Medium" | Procedures rewritten |
| 4 | `GET DIAGNOSTICS … ROW_COUNT` | Medium | `V_ROWS := SQLROWCOUNT` |
| 5 | `CONDITION FOR SQLSTATE` + `SIGNAL` | Medium | `DECLARE … EXCEPTION` + `RAISE` |
| 6 | `DAYS()` / `DIGITS()` — neither exists in Snowflake | Medium | `DATEDIFF`; `RIGHT(LPAD(TO_VARCHAR(ABS(x)),10,'0'),6)` |
| 7 | `IDENTITY(+1000, +1)` — `+` rejected | **None** | 6 de-signed |
| 8 | `ALTER COLUMN … RESTART WITH 6000` | Medium | Folded into `IDENTITY` start |
| 9 | `ENFORCED` (35), `ENABLE QUERY OPTIMIZATION` (11) | Partly (FDM) | Removed |
| 10 | `SSC-EWI-0035 "CHECK STATEMENT NOT SUPPORTED"` | — | **The EWI is wrong** (below) |
| 11 | `EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND` remapped to `42S02` | **None — silent logic bug** | Intent restored |

### Defect 10: `CHECK` constraints are supported and enforced

Verified: inserting `DISCOUNT_PCT = 250` into `PROMOTIONS` is rejected. All 11
check constraints were preserved. `ALTER TABLE … ADD CONSTRAINT … CHECK`
requires `ENABLE NOVALIDATE`, which skips validating existing rows but still
enforces new writes.

### Defect 11: the silent handler bug

DB2 used `EXIT HANDLER FOR NOT FOUND` (SQLSTATE `02000`, "no rows"). SnowConvert
emitted `WHEN OTHER EXIT THEN CASE WHEN SQLSTATE = '42S02'` — "table not found",
a different condition. The handler would fire only if `CUSTOMERS` were missing
and **never** when a customer did not exist. `SP_PLACE_ORDER` would silently

never became 1 — **an infinite `WHILE` loop**. Both now use cursor `FOR` loops.

## Procedure interface changes

Snowflake procedures take input-only parameters and return one value, so every

| Procedure | DB2 `OUT` | Snowflake |
|---|---|---|
| `SP_ADD_CUSTOMER` | `P_STATUS` | `RETURNS INTEGER` |
| `SP_REFRESH_CUSTOMER_SUMMARY` | `P_ROWS` | `RETURNS INTEGER` |
| `SP_UPDATE_CUSTOMER_ADDRESS` | `P_ROWS` | `RETURNS INTEGER` |
| `SP_RESTOCK_INVENTORY` | `P_NEW_ON_HAND` | `RETURNS INTEGER` |
| `SP_CHECK_INVENTORY_SHORTAGE` | count + deficit | `RETURNS OBJECT` |
| `SP_PLACE_ORDER` | order id + total | `RETURNS OBJECT` |

return `-1`, but Snowflake does not enforce primary keys so that could never
fire. The duplicate check is now an explicit `COUNT(*)` probe.

## Constraint semantics (each verified by execution)

| Constraint | Count | Declared | Enforced |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CHECK` | 11 | Yes | **Yes** |
| `PRIMARY KEY` | 11 | Metadata | **No** |
| `FOREIGN KEY` | 9 | Metadata | **No** |

### Lost `ON DELETE CASCADE` — mitigated

`LINES_INV_FK` (`INVOICE_LINES`→`INVOICES`) and `ITEMS_ORDER_FK`
(`ORDER_ITEMS`→`ORDERS`) were `ON DELETE CASCADE`. Snowflake ignores this, so a
parent delete orphans children with no error. Replaced by
`SP_DELETE_INVOICE(invno)` and `SP_DELETE_ORDER(order_id)`, which delete children
then parent in one transaction and roll back on error.

> These only help if callers use them. A plain `DELETE FROM INVOICES` still
> orphans children silently.

### Unenforced orphan prevention — risk accepted

| Constraint | Relationship | Covered? |
|---|---|---|
| `ORDERS_CUST_FK` | `ORDERS.CUSTNO` → `CUSTOMERS` | Yes — `SP_PLACE_ORDER` checks |
| `TXN_PROD_FK` | `INVENTORY_TRANSACTIONS.PRODUCT_ID` → `PRODUCTS` | Partly |

# DB2 → Snowflake Migration: `BIGDATA` Schema

**Date:** 11 Nov 2026 · **Source:** IBM DB2 12.1.5.0 (`testdb`) · **Target:** Snowflake `DB2_MIGRATION_SCRATCH.BIGDATA`

## Scope
30 objects in the `BIGDATA` schema: 11 tables, 8 views, 3 functions, 6 procedures, 2 sequences. `SALES_DEMO` excluded.

## Key constraint discovered
DB2 is a **conversion-only source** in AIM. Extraction, deployment, the object registry, assessment waves and orchestrated data migration are all unavailable — each confirmed by error code. DDL was produced with `db2look`; deployment was done manually.

## Work completed
- Extracted DDL from the DB2 container and converted via SnowConvert 2.51.1-Pr
- Repaired the converted output, which was **not deployable as delivered**
- Rewrote all 6 procedures for Snowflake Scripting
- Built `make_deployable.py` — a re-runnable transform applying ~116 mechanical fixes
- Deployed all 30 objects to Snowflake with zero errors
- Functionally verified every function and procedure, including error paths
- Committed and pushed to `github.com/JigneshBotla/DB2_Migration_2` branch `test`

## Converter defects found: 11
Only 4 carried an adequately severe warning. Notable:
- **56 Critical parse errors** from `db2look` scaffolding
- `IN`/`OUT` parameter modes, `GET DIAGNOSTICS`, `CONDITION`/`SIGNAL`, `DAYS()`, `DIGITS()` — all emitted but invalid in Snowflake
- `IDENTITY(+1000, +1)` — invalid, **no warning at all**
- `!!!RESOLVE EWI!!!` markers are not valid SQL
- `SSC-EWI-0035 "CHECK not supported"` is **wrong** — Snowflake supports and enforces `CHECK`

## Two silent logic bugs caught
1. `NOT FOUND` handler remapped to SQLSTATE `42S02` — `SP_PLACE_ORDER` would have **accepted orders for non-existent customers**
2. Same remapping on a cursor-exhaustion handler — **infinite `WHILE` loop**

Both would have passed deployment and failed in production.

## Constraint semantics verified
| Constraint | Count | Enforced |
|---|---|---|
| `CHECK` | 11 | **Yes** — all preserved |
| `PRIMARY KEY` | 11 | No |
| `FOREIGN KEY` | 9 | No |

Lost `ON DELETE CASCADE` on 2 relationships replaced by `SP_DELETE_INVOICE` / `SP_DELETE_ORDER`.

## Open items
1. **No data migrated** — all tables empty; manual `export` → `PUT` → `COPY INTO` required
2. 7 foreign keys unenforced — risk accepted
3. Cascade deletes depend on callers using the new procedures
4. `OUT` → return value is a **breaking change** for existing callers
5. No table-to-table lineage (lineage tracks data movement, not relationships)

## Reporting caveat
I issued three corrections to my own earlier statements during this work — on critical-issue counts, `CHECK` support, and a foreign-key count inflated by a bad `grep`. Figures in this summary are the verified ones.

1... # Customizing the migration plugin
2... 
3... The plugin walks each object through a sequence of tasks (register → convert → deploy → validate → ...). You can replace the skill that runs for any task with your own — useful when your team has a non-standard step (custom auth, in-house deploy tooling, extra validation, ...) without re-implementing the whole plugin.
4... 
5... This page is the contract you need: the list of overridable task ids, what each task is expected to do, and how to signal completion.
6... 
7... ## How to override a task
8... 
9... Drop a `SKILL.md` under either path; the plugin loads it instead of the built-in skill the next time that task runs.
10... 
11... | Path | When to use |
12... |---|---|
13... | `<project_dir>/.scai/skills/<task_id>/SKILL.md` | Override scoped to a single project. Project-local overrides take precedence. |
14... | `$AIM_SKILL_EXT_DIR/<task_id>/SKILL.md` | Set `AIM_SKILL_EXT_DIR` to a directory you maintain (e.g. a shared internal skills repo). Used as a fallback when the project does not carry the override. |
15... 
16... Your override SKILL.md is loaded as a normal agent skill — write it the same way you would any other skill. There is no template to subclass and no required imports.
17... 
18... To replace the entire `main` pipeline for one `customKind` (FiveTran, Airflow, …), discovery writes `<project_dir>/.scai/skills/<customKind>.md` with the customer — see [Custom code units](#custom-code-units-kindcustom). That is a file, not a `<task_id>/SKILL.md` directory.
19... 
20... To check what's currently in effect, run:
21... 
22... ```
23... migration_status(mode='extensions')
24... ```
25... 
26... It returns the catalog of every overridable task, the default executor the plugin would use, and the path of any active override.
27... 
28... ## How to exclude a task
29... 
30... Some tasks aren't relevant to every project. Disable one with the `configure` tool's `tasks` parameter — the plugin then treats it as `excluded` and follows the task's `excluded` branch instead of running it:
31... 
32... ```
33... configure(tasks={"validateView": false})
34... ```
35... 
36... The choice persists to `<project_dir>/.scai/config/plugin.yml` under `tasks.*`, so it holds across sessions.
37... 
38... - **Disable per-object tasks before registering any in-scope objects.** `main` tasks such as `validateView`, `migrateData`, and `validateData` are project-wide settings; new exclusions are rejected once an in-scope object is registered, including after a completed wave, so later waves cannot silently inherit them. Re-applying an existing disable is safe. One-time `setup` task exclusions are not subject to this timing guard.
39... - **Locked tasks can't be disabled.** Load-bearing steps are marked `locked` in the machine — `configure` rejects disabling them (the core setup steps, plus `registration`, `convert`, `deploy`, `etlStabilization`, `seedSynthetic`, `fixCode`).
40... - **Structural nodes can't be disabled.** Internal prompts, routers, and terminals have no executor to override — `configure` rejects attempts to exclude them too.
41... 
42... ## Task catalog
43... 
44... Tasks fall into two categories: `setup` (one-time per project) and `main` (per-object migration). Below is every task id you can override; internal routing nodes and setup prompts are not listed.
45... 
46... <cat>
47... 
48... ### `setup` (one-time per project)
49... 
50... | Task id | What it does |
51... |---|---|
52... | `dbtSetup` | Bootstraps a detected dbt project: resolves the source dialect from profiles.yml, initializes the project, and points the code-source step at local files so the generic dialect menu is never shown. |
53... | `midwayEntry` | Imports an existing pre-converted Snowflake project to be compatible with AIM projects. |
54... | `configureGit` | Configures git integration (main branch, remote, housekeeping commits). |
55... | `registerCode` | Pulls source SQL or ETL sources into the project. |
56... | `convertCode` | Runs the source → Snowflake conversion. |
57... | `dbtRepoint` | Agentic dbt repointing: validates and fixes dbt configs, macros, and refines converted SQL after the `--dbt` conversion. |
58... | `runAssessment` | Generates a migration assessment report. AIM overlays Q1 as next_prompt (assessment_options); assessment/SKILL.md skips its Step 3 confirmation when those tokens are set, then still gathers Discovery / Data Lineage inputs before the two-turn dispatch. |
59... | `configureSandboxProfile` | Configure a sandbox scai profile binding source and Snowflake target connections for iterative workload conversion. |
60... | `configureTesting` | Verifies the Snowflake side is ready for the chosen testing path (source data vs testbed). |
61... | `generateTestbed` | Bootstraps incremental testbed state from non-table coupling objects. Table CSVs are generated later by each table's deployCommonSandbox walker, in dependency order. On SQL Server, configure creates an empty AIMSBX_TB_* source catalog on the source connection and binds it in place of each self-mapped source: entry, and the rows load there. Other dialects, and a catalog configure could not create, keep the self-mapped entry: an extracted project then preserves its live source and loads no rows, and scai testbed load refuses any table holding rows it did not write. |
62... | `setupDataInfrastructure` | Configures the shared Data Migration & Validation infrastructure (compute pool for SPCS, or local) and generates the worker config, so it can be brought up at migration time with data_infrastructure(mode="up"). AIM overlays orchestrator/worker placement as next_prompt. |
63... | `dataStrategy` | Captures the project's data migration and validation strategy (migration type, sync strategy, extraction strategy, target table type; validation type + sync strategy) during setup so the choices are committed to the git main branch and shared with the team, instead of being decided ad hoc at first migration/validation. Snowflake-source projects skip the migration wizard and complete on validation type only. |
64... | `configureExtractionSource` | Configures the source database connection. |
65... 
66... ### `main` (per-object migration)
67... 
68... | Task id | What it does |
69... |---|---|

Creates the ephemeral `AIMSBX_*` catalogs unless a live leftover yaml already names a `ready` pair — then it does not DROP or CLONE. 87... | `migrateData` | Migrates data into a table. Interactive Iceberg tables skip `deploy` and reach this from `convert`; the orchestrator creates the database, schema, and Iceberg table here before loading.
